Volkswagen introduced the ID. Buzz Beach, a fun spin on its electric van that’s built for camping and overnight stays. However, it won’t be cheap, starting at over $70,000.
Meet the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach
Volkswagen’s original microbus became a cultural icon thanks to its open, customizable interior, making it perfect for large families, road trips, camping, and, of course, music festivals.
The ID. Buzz brings the classic Type 2 microbus into the electric era with a retro-new style, modern tech, and a flexible, spacious cabin.
Building on its reputation as a symbol of freedom and adventure, Volkswagen is adding a new member to the electric people mover lineup.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new ID. Buzz Beach “brings adventure into the electric age,” Volkswagen said after introducing the new variant on Thursday. Designed for camping, longer road trips, and overnight stays, the electric van will be available in 5-, 6-, and 7-seat configurations.
Volkswagen said it sleeps two comfortably with a removable bed frame and a custom-fitting folding mattress.
Volkswagen ID. Buzz Beach fold-out mattress (Source: VW UK)
The mattress is a decent size at about 6.5 feet long by 4 feet wide (2.0m x 1.2m), roughly the size of an average small double bed.
In the 5-seat configuration, the bed frame tucks away in the trunk, while in the 6- and 7-seat layouts, it’s stored vertically behind the third row of seats.
For camping and other longer stays, Volkswagen added a new Overnight mode that uses the vehicle’s battery to provide up to 48 hours of continuous, off-grid climate control. The new mode can be accessed on the center touchscreen.
It also includes blackout curtains throughout the cabin and ventilation grilles on the front side windows.
The ID. Buzz Beach offers vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities. A 230V power socket adaptor comes standard, letting you power an e-bike, charge a smartphone, run camping equipment, or power other external electronic devices. A camping connector is available as an added option.
To top it off, Volkswagen added a hidden foldable table and chairs set that can be tucked away without taking up internal space.
Volkswagen will open orders for the new ID. Buzz Beach in the UK later this month, starting at £53,955 (excluding VAT), or about $71,000. Including VAT and OTR costs, it will start at £65,837, or roughly $86,500.
What about those in the US? VW introduced the 2027 ID. Buzz with a new Tourer model that was essentially the same as the Beach variant in the UK, with a fold-out mattress, Overnight mode, blackout curtains, and a table and chairs set.
However, VW told its US dealers in September that it would be delaying the ID. Buzz’s return until the 2028 model year.
The 2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz started at about $60,000 in the US, which is one of the biggest reasons it failed to catch on with buyers. The original VW microbus was an affordable people mover.
A custom camper variant would likely cost more than $70,000. Would you pay $70,000 or more for Volkswagen’s electric camper van?

The go-ahead for Alnylam Pharmaceuticals–partnered Livsayis marks Regeneron’s second new modality this year after the company secured approval for hearing loss gene therapy Otarmeni in April.
Regeneron scored another first on Wednesday. Nearly seven months after getting the FDA’s nod for its first gene therapy, Regeneron and partner Alnylam Pharmaceuticals secured approval for Regeneron’s first siRNA therapy, which also happens to be a first-in-class option for generalized myasthenia gravis.
Late Wednesday evening, the FDA greenlit cemdisiran—to be marketed as Livsayis—for adults with gMG who are positive for anti-acetylcholine receptors. This is the most common type of the autoimmune disease, according to Regeneron’s release .
Truist Securities said the approval reflects progress stemming from Regeneron’s pipeline.
“In our view, the approval adds to REGN’s recent execution, with further revenue opportunities emerging from the pipeline alongside selective & disciplined external investment,” the analysts said in a Wednesday evening note.
GMG is a progressive disease characterized by muscle weakness that leads to difficulty talking, breathing, seeing and moving. A complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed siRNA, Livsayis reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, which is a key driver of the disease. It is also the only FDA-approved treatment for gMG to be administered subcutaneously four times a year, Regeneron said. Truist noted that this dosing provides “a practical point of differentiation.”
Analysts at BMO Capital Markets agreed, writing on Wednesday that the approval of Livsayis “establishes the asset as a first-in-class siRNA therapy for gMG, pairing best-in-class efficacy with quarterly subQ dosing to improve upon the patient experience.”
Livsayis was backed by the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial , during which the siRNA showed a 4.5-point improvement on a scale measuring how gMG symptoms affect daily functioning compared to a 2.2-point improvement for placebo at 24 weeks, meeting the primary endpoint. The drug also hit the trial’s key secondry endpoint, besting placebo on a clinician assessment of muscle function, with a 4.2-point improvement vs. a 1.5-point improvement with placebo.
Rare diseases
Regeneron Eyes 2026 Filing for siRNA Myasthenia Gravis Drug After Phase III Win
Regeneron’s cemdisiran, used alone or in combination with its complement inhibitor Veopoz, significantly improved activities of daily living in patients with generalized myasthenia gravis.
August 27, 2025
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
The therapy was tagged with a boxed warning—the FDA’s most severe caution—for serious meningococcal infections and other serious infections, which is “consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity,” Regeneron said. Truist said the warning was anticipated. The most common adverse reactions with Livsayis, affecting around 5% of those in NIMBLE, were injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections.
Livsayis is available only through a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program, which Regeneron said is also consistent with the class.
“As Regeneron’s first approved siRNA therapy, this approval marks a meaningful step forward for our neuroscience pipeline as we relentlessly pursue bold, new approaches to transform care for people living with serious neurological diseases,” Regeneron President and Chief Scientific Officer George D. Yancopoulos said in a prepared statement.
“All in,” BMO wrote, “[the] approval validates Regeneron’s siRNA platform and adds a modest growth driver to the company’s portfolio.”
The gMG win comes on the heels of the FDA’s April nod for Otarmeni , Regeneron’s first gene therapy and the first targeted treatment for congenital deafness caused by a deficiency of the otoferlin protein, which is critical to the hearing process.
Sandwiched in between these two firsts, Regeneron won approval for Pasatru in August. It was the second drug in the U.S. for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a rare bone disease, after Ipsen’s Sohonos, which debuted in 2023.
Gene therapy
FDA approval of Regeneron’s hearing loss gene therapy breaks barriers
Approved Thursday via the FDA’s Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher program, Otarmeni is the first gene therapy for hearing loss—and the first treatment to target an underlying cause of the condition.
April 23, 2026
·
4 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more

Hyundai’s electric SUVs are getting some love. The IONIQ 5 and three-row IONIQ 9 helped the Korean automaker land its first-ever “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” award from US News & World Report for 2027.
Is Hyundai the best EV brand in 2027?
“This win showcases the breadth and strength of Hyundai’s SUV and electric lineups,” Alex Kwanten, managing editor at Autos at US News , said after naming it the Best EV Brand and Best SUV Brand for 2027.
This marks the first time Hyundai has earned the Best EV Brand award and the third consecutive win for Best SUV Brand.
Including hybrid and electric vehicles, Hyundai offers ten unique SUVs, “many of them at or near the top of our rankings in those classes for capability, comfort, performance and value,” Kwanten said.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Hyundai’s fully electric SUVs, the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9, “in particular, stand out for their combination of style and technology,” he explained.
Hyundai currently offers the IONIQ 5, including the sporty IONIQ 5 N and off-road-focused IONIQ 5 XRT, plus the three-row IONIQ 9.
2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 (Source: Hyundai)
Although Hyundai discontinued its electric sedan, the IONIQ 6, after the 2025 model year, the new high-performance IONIQ 6 N joins the lineup in 2027.
Compact and three-row electric SUVs
The IONIQ 5 continued to earn praise, taking its third consecutive Best Compact Electric SUV award. Its larger sibling, the IONIQ 9, took the top spot in the midsize electric SUV category.
Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in the US this year through September that isn’t a Tesla, ranking third behind the Model Y and Model 3.
Why does it continue winning over buyers? The IONIQ 5 checks all the boxes with long-range capabilities, fast charging, and a surprisingly spacious interior with modern tech.
It’s also among the most affordable EVs in the US. Prices for the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 start at just $35,250.
However, the base price is for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, with prices starting at $37,750, but it offers up to 318 miles of range.

The three-row Hyundai IONIQ 9 electric SUV starts at $58,955 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles.
Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y, with two rows of seating and space for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating with six- or seven-seat options.
The larger IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with up to 106.5 cubic feet in the IONIQ 5.
Both electric SUVs use an 800-volt electrical architecture for ultra-fast charging. The IONIQ 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes, while the IONIQ 9 takes around 24 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.
Hyundai assembles the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.
When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told Electrek that its electric SUVs are winning over new buyers at a higher rate than any of its gas or hybrid vehicles.
Hyundai’s electric vehicle conquest rates (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek/ Hyundai)
The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

PARIS — France and Sweden held their first joint exercise under the forward deterrence initiative proposed by French President Emmanuel Macron, with French nuclear-capable Rafale jets and an Airbus A330 MRTT tanker aircraft operating over Sweden alongside Swedish Gripen fighters.
The exercise, dubbed Excalibur, was held in northern Sweden on Nov. 16 to 18, with the aim of improving interoperability between the French and Swedish air forces, the two countries’ armed forces said in statements on Thursday. The exercise didn’t involve actual nuclear weapons and was not directed at any country, the defense ministries said.
The French-Swedish cooperation follows an exercise last month in which British Eurofighter Typhoon jets escorted French Rafale jets on a simulated nuclear-strike mission . France has been working with several European allies to implement Macron’s proposal to bolster European deterrence , in the face of nuclear saber-rattling by Russia and uncertainty about United States security guarantees.
France’s nuclear deterrent consists of an ocean-based component comprising strategic ballistic-missile submarines, as well as an airborne component consisting of Rafale jets capable of carrying nuclear-tipped cruise missiles developed by MBDA.
“Since the in-depth dialogue on ‘forward deterrence’ was initiated, France and Sweden are taking steps to implement their common roadmap for strategic cooperation,” the Swedish Armed Forces said . The exercise “demonstrates our joint readiness and capability to act together and reflects the commitment of our two countries towards deterring threats and strengthening allied security.”
The deployment of the Rafale jets alongside Gripen fighters, with the support of an A330 MRTT, demonstrated the high level of interoperability between the two air forces in the areas of nuclear deterrence, in the service of Europe’s security, the French Armed Forces General Staff said in a post on the social network X .
“This type of deployment not only allows to test the dispersion of French aircraft to improve their capability to survive an adversary disabling strike, but also opens the door for new modes of operation previously unimaginable, such as attacking targets deep within the Russian Arctic or planning much smaller raids without needing in-flight refueling,” said Etienne Marcuz, a senior analyst at the Fondation pour la Recherche Stratégique, in a post on X.
Sweden’s Gripen fighters are “excellent combat aircraft” specifically designed to penetrate Russian ground-to-air and air-to-air defense systems, and they could be valuable assets during a nuclear strike mission, while freeing up conventional Rafale jets for other missions, Marcuz said.

Nate Watson’s case against the big supply chain software rollout comes down to timing. A team can spend 18 months spelling out its processes for a new system, he said, and its operations and partners will have changed by the time the system goes live. The time to value just doesn’t make sense.
Watson is chief commercial officer of Vantage 9 , a Bentonville, Arkansas, company that sells what it calls a composable supply chain platform. Its warehousing, inventory, order, yard and transportation functions come as prebuilt components that run on top of a company’s existing ERP, warehouse, and transportation management systems.
He made the argument in a FreightWaves Today interview on Oct. 28 at F3: Future of Freight Festival in Chattanooga, Tennessee, where AI adoption was one of the main themes on the agenda. Speakers kept returning to the same pressures, Watson said: AI, disruption in software-as-a-service and customers who expect their data to be integrated and secure.
“An 18 or 24 month supply chain system project just doesn’t make sense given the pace of change,” Watson said. “In talking with supply chain leaders, it’s clear that this approach is slow, often runs late, is expensive, and pulls staff away from their day jobs.”
The trouble starts in planning. “You work for 18 months saying, here’s my process. Here’s what I would need the system to do. Here’s the data and the reporting that I would need,” Watson said. “Well, 18 months in a supply chain is a lifetime. So you get to that go-live and then all of a sudden your operations have changed, your partners have changed.”
Custom code or a second vendor
A company that needs its ERP to handle 10% more than it does today has two options, Watson said: customize the system, which takes time and often specialized staff, or buy the missing capability from another vendor and run two products that do not communicate well.
“Customization is synonymous with expensive and slow,” Watson said. “Being able to deliver the value of custom at the speed of Saas is the problem Vantage 9 is out to solve.” Vantage 9 starts from the capabilities a customer needs, with the data flow and integrations already in place, so its team can concentrate on the screens operators will use.
“Everyone’s talked about an iterative and agile approach for years now,” Watson said. “It’s nothing new, but having the systems behind it that allow you to deliver that capability is new and is emerging.”
Prebuilt pieces on top of existing systems
Vantage 9 breaks the workload of the large systems into smaller components and assembles them for each customer.
“You can think about it like a Lego set,” Watson said. “We’ve broken down inventory management, order management, yard, warehousing, transportation functionality that you would turn to your systems for, and broken those down into individual capabilities, like a Lego piece.”
A large retailer might need three different warehouse management setups, Watson said, depending on the type of building and the partners each one serves. Each could draw on inventory functions and connect to the retailer’s transportation system or outside partners.
Customers can keep the systems they already run.
“If you have a system of record that’s doing the job 80 percent, that’s great,” Watson said. “With a composable platform, you’re able to leverage the very best of the systems that you already have in place, and then add in that 5, 10 percent where it’s missing.”
His example is a retailer that reconfigures a warehouse to handle product at a new temperature. The legacy warehouse management system may not have been designed for a last-in, first-out setup or for monitoring temperature changes. Vantage 9 would add the data management and the sensor integrations alongside it, he said, and each transportation provider or supplier added after that becomes easier to connect.
A company can also start with one warehouse type in one region and test it there without changing the system that manages the rest of the network.
Spreading the go-live out
Supply chains run 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and they cannot shut down for a technology upgrade, Watson said.
“So much of the challenge with these large system implementations is the people side. It’s the adoption. It’s slowing your operations so that you can go have a go-live for a new system or roll out new functionality,” he said.
A traditional cutover packs that change into one day: in Watson’s words, “you leave work Friday, work in one way, you show up Monday.” Adding capability in smaller steps spreads the training and change management over time and limits the disruption customers see, he said.
“If you have a big go-live and that’s disruptive to customers, it can be months before you regain that trust. That’s a business killer,” Watson said.
Vantage 9’s implementation team is made up of people who have worked in warehousing and transportation, Watson said, and it spends time on the floor learning “where’s the pallet loading, who’s running the dock.” That knowledge goes into the last 10% of each project, the interface warehouse staff actually work in.
One layer for people and AI agents
Watson sees the composable platform as the place where AI agents fit in. An executive might run a single process across five systems, he said, and what that executive cares about is the process and the outcome. The platform sits across those tools and sets data access, governance and permissions in one place.
“So whether it’s a human warehouse manager or their agent working on their behalf, our view is that in a composable platform, access to that data, the governance around that, the permissions, all needs to be set at a layer that’s not system-specific, that you can trade in and out those specific systems as needed as you get better capabilities from another,” he said.
From Firebend to Vantage 9
The company started in 2019 as Firebend, launched by a team of supply chain operators and technologists from Fort Smith, Arkansas, and spun out of Propak Corp.
Vantage 9 says its deployments are built to reach measurable return on investment within 90 days. The company says an unnamed national retailer saved more than $6 million in the first fiscal year, and it lists a 90% reduction in gate processing time and a 700% improvement in unload times among its results.
Two questions before a big purchase
Asked what an executive should consider before a large supply chain technology investment, Watson started with whether a new system is needed at all. The first question is whether an existing system can be modified or enhanced, and whether that saves money or time or helps the team more than a replacement would.
“Oftentimes we think, I don’t have the budget or the time to replace my system. But, if you can leverage what works well within you existing system, your focus becomes on small improvements that are faster and more cost effective.” The second is what sets the company up to keep improving over time.
“No one knows what technology is going to look like in two years, five years, ten years’ time,” Watson said. “Being in a posture where it’s easy for you to bring in the latest and best, but have that context of your organization and that data layer in place so that you can leverage new tools as they come out, allows you to experiment and innovate faster.”

EV Realty has broken ground on a 9 MW electric truck charging site in Torrance, California, that will have 50 charging ports when it opens to commercial fleets in mid-2027.
The company announced the groundbreaking Tuesday. Torrance is its second site in Southern California, after a 76-port hub in San Bernardino opened in April .
The hub is aimed at trucks serving the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, inland distribution centers, and air cargo around Los Angeles International Airport.
California Transportation Commission records show 20 of the 50 ports will use the Megawatt Charging System, or MCS, at up to 1.2 MW. The other 30 will be standard DC fast chargers at up to 350 kW. The site at 18715 S. Western Ave. sits beside Interstate 405 with a direct connection to Interstate 110.
Outpost, which has invested in EV Realty, added the 2.2-acre property to its truck terminal network in March and is a partner on the project along with ParWest and Synop.
Redesign added megawatt chargers
Under the commission’s original scope, the site would have had 60 ports, most rated at up to 300 kW, with 7.6 MW of total capacity. Commission records from March show EV Realty cut the count to 50 ports and raised capacity to 9 MW because the lower-power layout needed more space than the site had. Caltrans, which recommended the change, said the MCS ports would shorten charging times for trucks built to use them.
“With ultra-high-powered MCS charging, a drayage operator operating trucks from this site can run three, maybe even four turns per truck, per day, into the ports,” EV Realty CEO Patrick Sullivan said Tuesday at the groundbreaking. “That means more money and a more sustainable freight economy, with reduced local air impacts, for both the carriers and the shippers.”
The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach proposed in September paying zero-emission trucks $60 per terminal visit, up to $36,000 a year, under a three-year incentive program. In July, 613 such trucks called at the Port of Long Beach, according to port figures reported by Container News . That was nearly 3.6% of the 16,853 drayage trucks with access to San Pedro Bay terminals.
State grant covers part of the $22.1 million cost
The project’s budget is $22.1 million. A $7.9 million Trade Corridor Enhancement Program grant pays for part of construction, and EV Realty is covering the remaining $14.2 million. The cost rose from $18.37 million with the redesign, and EV Realty agreed to absorb the increase.
Southern California Edison’s fleet charging rebate and a conditional California Energy Commission award also support the project, in amounts the release does not give.
EV Realty buys sites where utility power is already available, an approach FreightWaves detailed in 2024 . The Torrance site has 9.9 MW of grid capacity, according to its state funding agreement.
“By providing access to power when and where it’s needed, we are addressing one of the primary constraints to electrification at scale,” Sullivan said in the release. “Our Powered Properties are ideally located to meet fleet operator needs, and all our sites have ready access to grid power without lengthy utility upgrades.”
An earlier state schedule had construction finishing Feb. 6, 2026. The end date is now June 30, 2027, after permitting delays at two outside agencies, including the city of Torrance.
The release does not name any fleets signed up for the Torrance site. The San Bernardino hub opened with J.B. Hunt, Gate City Beverage, and electric carrier Nevoya as customers.
Second site in a Southern California network
Beyond Torrance, EV Realty has announced future projects in Stockton and Ontario, California. The company said it is on track to have more than 100 MCS ports across Southern California by mid-2027.
“This site will connect with our San Bernardino charging hub, creating the beginning of our network in Southern California,” Chief Commercial Officer Suncheth Bhat said at the groundbreaking. “Being near the ports of LA and Long Beach, we are at the very epicenter of the movement of goods in this country. Few places in the country move more freight than where we are right now, and few places in the country are next door to a King’s Hawaiian, making this soon-to-be the best-smelling truck charging hub in the country.”
Next-generation trucks such as the Tesla Semi will be rolling out at scale when the site opens, the company said. Tesla plans to expand Semi deliveries next year after starting volume production in the third quarter.
“2027 is shaping up to be a year of real growth for this sector as truck technology continues to improve, charging networks expand in key freight hubs, and fleet operators see the potential to save money by going electric,” Bhat said in the release.
Why it matters: Drayage carriers at the San Pedro Bay ports weighing battery-electric trucks will have a shared megawatt-charging site near the terminals by mid-2027. Those buying at least 10 trucks can apply by Dec. 3 for up to $300,000 each from the Port of Los Angeles.

A Houston ship pilot has been indicted on a federal seaman’s manslaughter charge stemming from a 2024 collision in the Houston Ship Channel that killed a sailor, marking what authorities say is the first prosecution of its kind against a ship pilot in U.S. history.
Darris Ornel Jefferson, 39, is accused of misconduct, negligence and inattention while piloting the Chinese bulk carrier Yangze 7 through the Houston Ship Channel on July 19, 2024, according to an indictment announced Wednesday.
The charges allege Jefferson’s actions caused the death of a crew member aboard the towing vessel Miss Peggy , which collided with the bulk carrier near Lynchburg, Texas.
Jefferson is scheduled to make his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Christina Bryan on Nov. 24 at 2 p.m.
If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in federal prison and a $250,000 fine.
The indictment follows a National Transportation Safety Board investigation that concluded cellphone distraction and failure to maintain a proper lookout caused the fatal collision.
NTSB investigation cited cellphone distraction
According to the NTSB’s findings released Aug. 6, the Yangze 7 and Miss Peggy were both traveling inbound through the Houston Ship Channel when they collided.
The impact caused the Miss Peggy to capsize and sink with five crew members aboard.
Four crew members were rescued by another vessel, including one who suffered serious injuries. The fifth crew member was later found dead inside the wreckage.
NTSB investigators determined that the pilot directing the Yangze 7 had been engaged in a nonoperational cellphone conversation with another ship pilot for approximately 39 minutes before the collision.
The phone call ended just two minutes and 16 seconds before the crash.
Investigators concluded the conversation distracted the pilot from his navigation responsibilities, leaving him unaware of the Miss Peggy’s presence.
The investigation also found that neither vessel maintained a proper lookout while navigating the channel.
The captain of the Miss Peggy failed to detect the approaching Yangze 7 from behind, while the bulk carrier’s bridge team did not detect the towboat until it was less than one ship’s length ahead, according to the NTSB.
The NTSB determined that distraction and failure to maintain a proper lookout were the probable causes of the collision.
Federal officials emphasize maritime safety
The criminal indictment represents an unusual escalation in federal enforcement following a fatal commercial maritime accident.
Officials said the case marks the first time a ship pilot has faced federal seaman’s manslaughter charges .
“The tragic loss of life shows the serious consequences that can result when a mariner does not carry out their duties with proper care and attention,” said Damon J. Youmans, special agent in charge of the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service’s Gulf Field Office.
Why it matters: The federal criminal case against a Houston ship pilot could intensify scrutiny of navigation practices, cellphone use and accountability for maritime accidents at major U.S. shipping gateways.

Musk Hints at More Tesla Lineup Culling, Model Y Will Only Be a Seven-Seater With No Steering Wheel

Photo: Tesla
After sounding the death knell for the Model S, Model X, and then the Cybertruck, Elon Musk now wants Tesla to trim the Model Y lineup. In a recent interview, he said that demand for the long-wheelbase variant Model Y L is so strong that Tesla could drop all other trims. This will eventually be the only Model Y available, and it won't have a steering wheel and pedals, just like the Cybercab.
Tesla is holding a shareholder meeting on December 3, and it's all about giving Elon Musk more power. Officially, the agenda includes the re-election of Musk, Robyn Denholm, and JB Straubel to the Board of Directors and the approval of the 2025 executive compensation package, including about $158.4 billion in 2025 stock awards to Musk.
Unofficially, the meeting will give more power to Musk and the board by debuting the automatic voting, or Tesla's Voluntary Retail Voting Program. This essentially locks investor votes with the board for future votes if they agree to participate. It is also expected that Musk will officially announce a future merger with SpaceX .
More importantly, Musk will use the meeting to double down on his plans for Tesla to phase out vehicle manufacturing. He said a while back that the Roadster would be the last driver's car from Tesla, and he appears to do whatever he can to keep his promise. That is, if Tesla shareholders don't stop this madness.
Musk has started by culling Tesla's lineup, first by killing the Model S and Model X earlier this year. The Cybertruck followed shortly, with the stainless steel truck slated for an untimely demise next summer. Although it was obvious that the Model 3 might follow next, it appears that not even the Model Y is safe from the axe.
Photo: Tesla During a recent interview at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk said that the demand for the long-wheelbase Model Y L is off the charts. That's the good part. The bad part is that Musk has gotten the idea that Tesla should stop building all other variants of the Model Y and focus its entire production on the Model Y L.
If that wasn't controversial enough, Musk went on to say that people won't be able to drive this Model Y variant in the near future. Instead, Musk said that Tesla would build an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have a steering wheel or pedals. That's the same Model Y L, though, because he also said that this autonomous variant should be able to transport groups of six or seven people.
So, there you have it, folks, another installment of the same "Tesla is not a carmaker" franchise. I'm not sure what timeline Musk set for these changes. From where I stand, it appears that he is already planning for a world without human drivers, even if autonomous vehicles are only allowed in some small areas in a few cities in the world. Wiping out the entire Tesla's vehicle lineup to build more parking lot decorations seems like a sure way of ensuring that Tesla doesn't survive .
As for when the Model 3 will disappear, it suffices to say that the sedan doesn't address any untapped transportation needs. The Cybercab is cheap to build and convenient to operate, while the Model Y has the advantage of accommodating more passengers, but the Model 3? It has a target on its back already. Elon says @Tesla will introduce a fully autonomous version of the Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals: "It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people. We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got 4 or 6, or a whole family. What we plan to do is have an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people." (via NYT Dealbook Summit today) — Sawyer Merritt (@SawyerMerritt) November 18, 2026

With Kisqali going off patent and decreasing prices impacting sales, Novartis has narrowed sales guidance to 5% growth. But management remains steadfast that they have a plan to get back on track.
For a long time, Novartis has looked to Cosentyx and Kisqali for growth into the next decade. But today, the Swiss pharma set out more modest sales guidance than analysts hoped at 5% growth through 2031. As one legendary analyst put it, “the pluses are all gone today.”
Novartis hosted an investors day on Thursday, revealing the company’s outlook for 2026 through 2031. Instead of Kisqali and Cosentyx playing a starring role, Novartis hiked sales guidance for Kesimpta to $8 billion and Scemblix and Leqvio to $5 billion each. Sales projections for 2025-2030, set last year, came in the at the low end of the previously forecast growth rate of 5-6% .
The difference in 2031 comes down to the entry of generics, which will begin to weigh on Novartis’ portfolio and lead to lowered expectations for some key products for that year.
Cosentyx, which is approved for multiple immune-mediated inflammatory diseases like psoriasis, is expected to peak in 2027, CEO Vas Narasimhan said on a call with analysts. The drug brought in $6.67 billion for 2025 , marking a 9% year-over-year increase. The breast cancer medicine Kisqali, meanwhile, collected $4.78 billion last year.
Narasimhan blamed price declines from the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) that will begin for Cosentyx in 2028, followed by loss of exclusivity in 2029.

Kisqali on the other hand will similarly see an IRA-driven price decline in 2028 but the CEO expects the drug to return to growth afterward, with sales potential of $10 billion “in the 2030 period.” The company last year listed sales expectations at $10 billion-plus for that same time period.
And that’s why TD Cowen’s legendary analyst Steve Scala, who appears on many major pharma earnings calls with sharp questions , wondered about the pluses, which did not appear on this year’s release. Does Novartis now think the drug will not grow beyond $10 billion? Narasimhan insisted it was “a policy decision just to remove pluses” rather than one pointing to lowered expectations.
“When you have an expiry like Kisqali, you will go down on growth rates, but you all know that. I mean that’s just normal in this sector,” Narasimhan said. “The real question is, do you have the replacement power to come back out? And we believe we’re showing you that we do.”
No big deal
Novartis shares declined for the second day in a row on Thursday, falling about 2.6% to $151.18. The company has had a tumultuous year, with multiple Phase 3 clinical failures for acquired products like Avidity Biosciences’ main asset del-desiran. The highly anticipated cardiovascular drug pelacarsen also failed .
Executives headed into the investor day hoping to assuage fears about the company’s future. Analysts probed Narasimhan and his team about what assets might be missing from their expectations for post-2030.
The CEO pointed to remibrutinib , pelabresib and ianalumab as assets with multibillion-dollar potential.
“If you’re missing $10 billion in 2035 and you can’t get there with the size of our pipeline, then your probabilities are wrong, right? They’re just wrong,” Narasimhan said. “It just takes two or three of these to hit and you get there.”

Novartis is expected to grow on average in the mid-single digits through 2031, with core operating income margin to return to 40% or more by 2029. While Novartis reported a margin of 41% in the third quarter, the number is expected to dip in the years to come by at least 2% with the patent and pricing headwinds, CFO Mukul Mehta explained.
And that’s just based on existing internal programs. “There’s no assumption of a big M&A deal,” Narasimhan said. “We have conviction because of all the assets that you’ve seen here that we already have in the organization.”
That said, Narasimhan and Ronny Gal, chief strategy and growth officer, expect M&A to add to the company’s portfolio over the next nine years, while the company works to keep R&D costs in check while delivering on the pipeline.
Specifically, Novartis will be looking for several smaller to mid-sized deals, particularly $2 billion or less, for early-stage research, Gal said. “We expect, long term, about half of our revenue to come from external assets.”

Entry-Level Bonneville T40 Lands in April 2027 as One of the Cheapest Triumph Motorcycles Around
55 photos
Photo: Triumph
A little more than a month after it released the full details of a newcomer in the Bonneville family, British bike maker Triumph finally announced when the new bike will become available at dealers, but also how much it will cost – for now, only on the home market.
The new Bonneville , which is now the entry-level bike in the family, comes in two flavors, T40 and T40 Black. They will both be on dealers' floors as soon as April 2027 (a bit later than I expected, to be honest), and they carry a sticker that reads £5,995 in the UK.
The price for the American market is not yet known, but so that you can form an idea, I'll tell you that price equates to $7,862 at today's exchange rates. No matter how you twist it, this makes the T40 one of the most affordable Triumph motorcycles around.
So, what does one get for such a low sum? First of all, a dedicated chassis that relies on the same 400cc TR Series engine that powers the Speed 400, Scrambler 400 X, Scrambler 400 XC, Tracker 400, and Thruxton 400 .
The powerplant has been modified for use in the new bike, and it now comes with a unique engine tune, revised cylinder head, and machined cooling heads. In this application, the powertrain is good for 32 hp at 7,000 rpm and 36 Nm of torque at 5,000 rpm – making it a perfect choice for both experienced riders and A2 license holders.
The bike's suspension system comprises the classic fork design at the front and twin shocks at the rear, which tie into an 18-inch and a 17-inch wheel, respectively, both of them featuring aluminum rims.
Triumph spent a lot of time making the T40 and its T40 Black offshoot look as close as possible to the other members of the Bonneville family, while at the same time paying tribute to the versions from the past, especially the ones from the 1960s.
The two-wheelers come with a teardrop fuel tank, a round LED headlight, and a brushed peashooter silencer slapped onto the exhaust system. Aluminum highlights the bikes' engine covers, clutch, and alternator, while the mirrors and grab hoop are chrome-finished.
Triumph will be selling the bikes in one of three two-tone color schemes, namely Aegean Blue and Fusion White, Meriden Blue and Tangerine Orange, and New England White and Jet Black. The single-color options come as Matt Pewter Grey and Matt Phantom Black.
Put together with assistance from Indian partner Bajaj , the T40 and T40 Black don't cut corners when it comes to safety systems, despite their low price. As such, it offers the blessings of five riding modes, cruise control, cornering ABS, and optimized cornering traction control, among others.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 19, 2026
Developer Vizsla Silver (TSX, NYSE American: VZLA) has pushed back its target for first production at the Panuco project in Mexico by a year as it prepares for a phased return to the site following the abduction and killing of 10 workers in Sinaloa. The stock dropped. Vancouver-based Vizsla now targets first silver in the second half of 2028, according to a statement Thursday. Engineering is about halfway complete and about 85% of the planned processing plant equipment has been ordered. Permitting, site readiness and construction timing figured in the revised schedule. “We stand by the families of our colleagues and share their grief in this profound loss, as well as their need for answers,” CEO Michael Konnert said in the release.
Vizsla shares dropped 2.3% to $4.16 Thursday morning in Toronto, having earlier dropped as low as $3.86. That values the company at about $1.5 billion (US$1 billion).
Community foundation
Gunmen abducted the Vizsla workers in the municipality of Concordia on Jan. 23. The remains of the last missing worker were identified in July, Mexican newspaper El Independiente reported.
Vizsla has committed US$5 million to a foundation for communities in Sinaloa and plans to contribute a share of future profits. The foundation would supplement the company’s direct assistance to affected families. Mexican federal authorities announced arrests in connection with the case in September. In October, Mexico’s defence ministry reported further arrests and said it had linked those detained to the abductions and killings. Vizsla says it continues to assist the investigation.
Two mines
Silver and gold mining in the Panuco-Copala district dates back centuries. Vizsla began exploring there in 2019 and moved to consolidate ownership of the district in 2021 by exercising two options. Its current mine plan calls for two underground mines, Copala and Napoleon, feeding a single plant. Security concerns had already interrupted work at Panuco. Vizsla paused fieldwork in April 2025 and resumed it the following month.
After the January abductions, the company again suspended some work at and near the site while engineering continued remotely. Vizsla says it’s working with Mexican federal authorities and security advisers on a phased return.
Approvals needed
Panuco still needs key federal approvals. Vizsla submitted its environmental impact assessment in February 2025 and said in its annual filing that Mexico’s environment ministry had asked for more information. A land-use change authorization is also required before construction. Vizsla has yet to make a production decision. Its November 2025 feasibility study put initial capital at US$238.7 million and projected payable output of 94.7 million oz. of silver and 776,000 oz. of gold over 9.4 years. The study’s estimates don’t reflect the revised schedule, potential cost increases or financing costs.

Actinogen Medical’s lead program for its sole pipeline candidate has failed a late-stage study, but the Australian biotech still plans on taking the findings to the FDA for a path forward.
Actinogen Medical’s experimental oral therapy failed to slow decline for patients with Alzheimer’s disease in a pivotal study, though the biotech is touting findings from a subgroup as a potential path ahead.
The Australian biotech’s stock crashed more than 80% on the news and is currently worth less than 1¢ in USD.
Actinogen evaluated Xanamem, also known as emestedastat, in 247 patients with mild to moderate Alzheimer’s disease (AD) who also had elevated levels of the pTau181 blood biomarker. The once-daily pill is designed to selectively control cortisol levels in the brain, liver and fat by blocking the enzyme 11β-HSD1.
In the Phase 2b/3 trial , Xanamem failed to delay disease progression compared to placebo, according to a Thursday release . The drug was tied to a mean benefit of 0.10 points as measured by a clinical dementia scale at week 36, a measure that wasn’t statistically significant.
The biotech also said that “small and non-significant trends favoring Xanamem” were observed on secondary endpoints assessing cognition and daily life activities.
Actinogen instead trumpeted results from a subpopulation of patients older than 75 years, in which disease was slowed by 0.39 points, or 30%, at week 36, as measured by the clinical dementia scale. The biotech compared this rate to currently approved drugs, with Biogen and Eisai’s Leqembi and Eli Lilly’s Kisunla achieving a 27% and 29% slowing of decline in late-stage trials at 18 months and 17.4 months, respectively.

Epic Gold (CSE: EPG; US-OTC: NFLDF) has established its first gold resources at the Wilson and Fenton properties in Quebec’s Abitibi greenstone belt, giving the explorer a basis for expansion drilling at both projects.
Wilson holds an estimated 279,000 inferred oz. gold, compared with 90,000 inferred oz. for Fenton, Epic said Thursday. Nearly three-quarters of Wilson’s gold falls within conceptual open-pit reporting limits.
Located 15 km east of Lebel-sur-Quévillon, Wilson has inferred resources of 3.05 million tonnes at 2.85 grams gold per tonne. Of that, 2.41 million tonnes at 2.66 grams for 205,000 oz. sit within the projected open pit, while the underground portion holds 642,000 inferred tonnes at 3.57 grams for 74,000 ounces.
Wilson’s initial resource “provides a meaningful starting point for evaluating the project,” CEO Rod Husband said in the statement. “Importantly, the estimate incorporates both open-pit and underground reporting constraints, providing a framework for understanding the distribution of mineralization and assessing future exploration priorities.”
As for Fenton, Epic’s geological interpretation “indicates that mineralization extends beyond the current resource constraints, highlighting opportunities for further discovery,” said exploration vice-president Mark Richardson.
Fenton is estimated to hold inferred resources of 1.92 million tonnes at 1.46 grams gold per tonne. Both estimates, effective Nov. 9, used a long-term gold price of $3,600 (C$5,148) an oz., assumed 92% recovery and drew on historical drilling. The figures come a day after Epic disclosed an update resource for its third Quebec project, Benoist, which put indicated gold at 150,700 oz. and inferred gold at 86,900 ounces.
Former Exploits
Formerly named Exploits Discovery, the company adopted the Epic name earlier this year. Its shares began trading Feb. 18 as it focused on a portfolio spanning Ontario and Quebec.
The Quebec properties came through a 2025 option agreement with Cartier Resources (TSXV: ECR) to earn up to a 100% interest in Wilson, Fenton and Benoist through cash payments, share issuances and exploration spending.
At Fenton, Epic completed 4,259 metres of drilling in 10 holes this year. Results released in May included 5.85 metres grading 4.65 grams gold per tonne at the Everest target and 76.8 metres at 1.23 grams at Fenton Main. The intervals are drilled lengths; true widths remain unknown.
Epic also reported a current resource at its optioned Hawkins project in Ontario in October: about 14 million inferred tonnes grading 0.98 gram gold per tonne for 440,000 oz. The McKinnon deposit lies about 80 km south-southwest of Hearst. Together with Benoist, Wilson and Fenton, it gives Epic current resource estimates at all four projects.
Shares of Epic dropped 9.5% to C19¢ Thursday afternoon, valuing the company at about C$12.7 million ($8.9 million). The stock has traded between C16¢ and C38¢ since Epic went public.

Yukon Is a Dual-Loft Tiny Home That Feels Like a Cozy Retreat on Wheels for Four
27 photos
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes
Tiny houses are not a mainstream housing option just yet, but they are certainly attracting more attention from people seeking more affordable, sustainable, and minimalist ways to live. Rising property prices and a growing desire for more freedom, both personal and financial, have made compact homes an appealing alternative to traditional housing.
As interest in tiny homes continues to rise, manufacturers feel motivated to come up with increasingly versatile designs that offer comfort, style, and practical features. Today, tiny houses come in all shapes and sizes, but two-loft models that maximize vertical space and create separate sleeping and storage zones while keeping the main floor open for daily living remain among the most flexible designs.
The Yukon tiny house on wheels perfectly exemplifies this flexibility. With its traditional layout that keeps the common, social areas downstairs and puts the sleeping areas at loft level at opposing ends of the house, this model can adapt to different needs and lifestyles, accommodating couples, roommates, hosts, and even families.
This tiny home is designed and built by Amberwood Tiny Homes, a Canadian manufacturer based in Bow Island, Alberta. Part of the Hiebert Group, the company operates under its current name since spring 2025, but it has actually been in business since 2022. It offers several types of compact dwellings, including tiny homes on wheels, foundation-built tiny homes, and park model homes , each designed to offer quality, comfort, and year-round livability.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes Described as a modern farmhouse-style tiny house, the Yukon combines the classic dual-loft layout with practical amenities and eye-pleasing aesthetics. It is perched on a triple-axle trailer and measures 28 feet (8.5 meters) long and 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide, which means it stays within legal dimensions for road transportation without special permits.
Its design is rooted in minimalism, but the included amenities and easy-to-navigate configuration make it just as comfortable and practical as a full-size home. The first thing that showcases this home’s mix of simplicity and elegance is the exterior, which is clad in white vertical board-and-batten siding, complemented by a roof design that adds some architectural character.
A central sloped roof is flanked by two elevated, flat-roofed sections, and the entire surface is finished in black standing-seam metal. Black-framed windows dot the facades, and a blue entry door adds a splash of color.
Yukon’s interior boasts a modern, minimalist, and functional design , with a calm, coastal-farmhouse aesthetic that pairs clean lines with a beautiful palette of white, warm wood tones, muted gray, deep navy blue, and earthy neutrals. The white shiplap walls, a vaulted ceiling in the center of the house, and multiple windows keep the space open and bright, while premium finishes, like natural wood planks on the ceilings, quartz countertops, and luxury vinyl flooring throughout, ensure beauty, durability, and low maintenance.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes With a footprint of just 362 square feet (33.6 square meters), the interior is compact, but the open, linear layout makes good use of the available space, creating a nice habitat that can accommodate up to four people. Comprising an inviting living room, a full kitchen, a dedicated dining area, and two opposing lofts, it truly makes the most of its compact dimensions. What’s more, the full kitchen and bathroom, modern appliances, washer/dryer combo, and four-season design make it feel like a true home.
One of the things that the Yukon does differently from other tiny houses is the access to the lofts. The stairs leading to the main sleeping loft are positioned toward the rear of the house rather than taking up valuable space in the middle of the home. This arrangement leaves space for an open central living area and makes the interior feel more comfortable by improving circulation between the essential zones.
Made from beautiful stained wood, the staircase is also a statement piece. Instead of traditional spindles, it features a solid panel balustrade, and its space-saving L-shaped design makes it easy to climb. In addition, it serves as extra storage space, with the lower steps hiding handy drawers and the underside configured with open shelves. Snug yet open and welcoming, the living room is fitted with a full-size sofa, offering a comfortable place to relax. The adjacent full kitchen is designed with full-time living in mind, featuring all the essentials for everyday meals.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes It’s really stylish, too, with navy blue lower cabinets and white upper cabinetry, complemented by gray solid surface countertops and stainless-steel appliances. A deep sink, four-burner cooktop, oven, range hood, and full-size fridge make it entirely modern in terms of functionality.
Another aspect that makes this home more livable than other models of the same size is the inclusion of a dedicated dining space. While many tiny houses rely on a basic breakfast bar or a counter extension for dining, the Yukon features a comfortable dining area for four people with an elegant round table, a built-in bench, and additional chairs that match the lounge sofa.
The dual-loft configuration offers flexibility in terms of sleeping arrangements, with both elevated areas luminous and spacious enough to accommodate double mattresses. If you don’t need extra sleeping capacity, one of the lofts can even be configured as a workspace, extra lounge, reading corner, or used for storage.
Photo: Amberwood Tiny Homes As for Yukon’s bathroom, it is just as functional as the rest of the house, with a vanity, a toilet, a walk-in shower, and some open cubbies for linen and toiletries. In the hallway, there is even a dedicated space for a washer and dryer, along with a full-height closet.
As mentioned, this is a tiny home that you can live in permanently, with quality insulation, in-floor heating, air conditioning, LED lighting, and many of the conveniences you would expect in a conventional home. For utilities, it comes with RV hookups, and like all the models in Amberwood’s lineup, the Yukon can be converted into a permanent foundation build if you’d rather place it in a fixed location.
The Yukon tiny house on wheels is listed at CAD$156,726 (USD $109,567) plus taxes, and the company delivers anywhere in Canada or the United States.

2027 Hyundai Elantra Officially Unveiled in Los Angeles: It's Longer, Wider, Taller, Smarter
11 photos
Photo: Hyundai
While SUVs and pickup trucks get all the attention in America, Hyundai proves that sedans are still alive with the all-new Elantra, one of the best-selling models in the segment in the U.S. Here comes the all-new, eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra, alongside the 2028 Elantra Hybrid. Both were unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show, just miles from the brand’s U.S. headquarters.
They call it Elantra, i30, and Avante . Its name depends on who you ask and where you buy it from. Regardless of the name, the model has been completely redesigned. It grew in all directions, it got a sharper look, and it received new tech.
The eighth-generation 2027 Hyundai Elantra is significantly larger than the outgoing model, stretching 3.4 inches (85 millimeters) longer, 1.2 inches (30 millimeters) wider, 0.4 inches (10 millimeters) taller, and riding on a 1.2-inch longer wheelbase, which translates to more legroom, shoulder room, and headroom for those sitting in the back.
In the meantime, the Elantra is keeping its exterior footprint in the compact class, where it is ready to give the Toyota Corolla and the Honda Civic a run for their money in the compact sedan segment in the United States.
Photo: Hyundai The car follows Hyundai's new "Art of Steel" design language. The redesigned silhouette trades the previous generation’s soft curves for sharper lines, muscular fenders, and flush-mounted door handles. It all starts with the H-shaped LED lighting signature at both ends, something that we first saw in the Hyundai Santa Fe SUV .
The new Hyundai Elantra gets the firm’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment system, Pleos Connect, running on a standard 12.9-inch central touchscreen. It supports over-the-air updates, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and the optional LLM-powered voice assistant called Gleo AI.
Yet, the model retains something that other automakers are returning to after years of transferring all functions to touchscreens. The 2027 Hyundai Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid will get physical climate and audio knobs, as executives say driving the sedan is an "eyes on the road, hands on the wheel" experience.
The slim digital instrument cluster sits near the base of the windshield, displaying relevant driving data. The gearbox shifter migrated to the steering column, freeing up space in the center console for dual wireless charging pads. The options list includes a Bang & Olufsen sound system and second-row air vents.
Photo: Hyundai The powertrain of the new generation won’t make headlines. The 2027 Hyundai Elantra retains the naturally aspirated 2.0-liter Smartstream inline-four and Intelligent Variable Transmission ( IVT ), producing 147 horsepower (149 metric horsepower) and 132 pound-feet (179 Newton meters) of torque. An N variant should arrive at a later date with more oomph, but nope, Hyundai isn't planning an Elantra station wagon .
In the meantime, the 2028 Elantra Hybrid will come with the 1.6-liter inline four and an electric motor for a combined output of 155 horsepower (157 metric horsepower). Hyundai hasn't disclosed the torque figure of the hybrid Elantra yet. A six-speed dual-clutch transmission puts the power down. Both powetrains operate in a front-wheel-drive setup.
The price has yet to be announced. Hyundai will disclose the missing numbers closer to the launch date. To keep the Elantra competitive in the United States, Hyundai will have to position it very close to its main rivals in the compact segment: the Toyota Corolla starts at $23,125, while the Corolla Hybrid is a $24,975 deal. In the meantime, the Honda Civic kicks off at $24,695 and the Civic Hybrid is a $29,395 deal.

Image: Fang Cheng Bao
BYD launched a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard. It comes standard on the top trim of the Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, which sells for 329,900 yuan (about $49,000) in China.
Automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade. This is the first one customers can actually order, according to BYD.
How BYD’s folding steering wheel works
The whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire. There’s no steering column physically connecting the wheel to the front wheels, so the wheel is just an input device, and BYD can put it wherever it wants.
The Tai 9’s steering wheel folding into the dash and back out. GIF made from Fang Cheng Bao’s official video.
On the Tai 9, it swings through 180 degrees on a hidden hinge and drops into a compartment in the dash in about 10 seconds. A panel closes over it, and a tray table folds out where the wheel used to be. Only the airbag remains outside of the compartment – keeping it useful with the steering wheel deployed or hidden.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The driver’s side with the wheel stowed. Image: Fang Cheng Bao
It only folds when the vehicle is parked. Fang Cheng Bao pairs it with a driver’s seat that reclines to 165 degrees, so the pitch is simple: fold the wheel, lie back, and eat, nap, or play games while you charge or wait. The brand claims 80% of the driver’s area becomes usable space and rates the folding mechanism for 80,000 cycles.
When it’s deployed, it’s a regular D-shaped wheel with a full rim and physical buttons. No yoke. That’s a nice change from Tesla and Mercedes, which paired its new steer-by-wire system on the EQS with a yoke .
The wheel in driving position. Image: Fang Cheng Bao
At the launch event, Fang Cheng Bao general manager Xiong Tianbo said the industry had been talking about folding steering wheels since 2016 without ever getting one into mass production. He added that BYD is using the same type of motor it develops for humanoid robots to move the wheel, a first in one of its cars.
Here’s Fang Cheng Bao’s official video of the feature:
Fang Cheng Bao’s official video of the Tai 9’s folding cabin (in Chinese)
Why it’s happening now
China’s new national standard for steering systems took effect on July 1, 2026. It dropped the long-standing requirement for a mechanical link between the steering wheel and the road wheels, as long as the system meets redundancy and fail-safe rules.
Before that, steer-by-wire needed special approval. Nio’s ET9 was the first car in China to get it, back in December 2024. In the US, Tesla’s Cybertruck already uses it, and Mercedes is bringing it to the EQS this year.
The Tai 9’s chassis with the steer-by-wire steering wheel unit. Image: Fang Cheng Bao
Folding wheels themselves have stayed on show stands. BYD’s own Denza brand showed one on the Z concept at Shanghai in 2025. Autoliv and Tensor called theirs the “world’s first foldable steering wheel” at CES in January, for a Tensor Robocar they expected to reach volume production in the second half of 2026. Hyundai Mobis has been showing one for years.
Tesla went the other way with the Cybercab: no wheel at all. But the prototypes testing on public roads have a Cybertruck steering wheel bolted onto an exposed column , because a human still has to be able to drive.
The rest of the Tai 9
The Tai 9 is Fang Cheng Bao’s biggest SUV yet. It’s 5,270 mm (207.5 in) long with a 3,130 mm wheelbase and six seats in a 2+2+2 layout. It’s also the first model on BYD’s new DMS hybrid platform.
A 1.5-liter turbo engine works with front and rear electric motors for a combined 400 kW (536 hp), and 0 to 100 km/h takes 4.8 seconds. The 66.48 kWh second-generation Blade battery supports BYD’s flash charging and delivers 310 km (193 miles) of electric range on the WLTC cycle. Rear-wheel steering, LiDAR, and BYD’s God’s Eye B driver assistance system are standard.
The Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9. Image: Fang Cheng Bao
There are three trims: 279,900 yuan (about $41,700), 299,900 yuan, and 329,900 yuan. Only the top one gets the folding wheel.
Fang Cheng Bao sold 43,872 vehicles in October, up 41% year-over-year, mostly on the strength of the Tai 7. That model is now heading overseas: BYD sells it in the UK as the Ti 7 . BYD hasn’t said anything about exporting the Tai 9.

It is not only that these technologies are impressive, but it is the speed at which they are being put into market by some of these Chinese car companies like BYD. They are moving further and further away from the competition but its understandable with the insane competition between car makers in China that they almost have to maintain and edge.

We’ve seen this at pretty much every auto show since the mid-2010s: a steering wheel slides away so the “driver” can relax while the car drives itself. It never shipped, for many reasons, but with steer-by-wire and autonomous driving now becoming reality, BYD is making the jump.
The Tai 9’s wheel only folds when you’re parked, so right now it’s a lounge feature. Recline the seat, stow the wheel, flip out the tray, and watch a movie while you charge. Is that a gimmick? A little. But Chinese EV buyers spend a lot of time in parked cars, and fridges, screens, and lie-flat seats sell cars there for a reason.
The bigger deal is underneath. The wheel can only fold because the Tai 9 is steer-by-wire, and BYD is putting that in a roughly $49,000 family SUV less than five months after China made it legal. After Cybertruck and now Mercedes with the EQS, we might be seeing the first steps of steer-by-wire actually becoming a more widely adopted technology.

Man Buys New 2026 Ford F-150 Raptor R for $117,520, Drives 2,200 Miles, Sells for $118,000
28 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Remember when you could buy a brand-new F-150 Raptor R, drive it around for a few months, and then sell it for considerably more than what you originally paid? Well, it's possible those days might be coming to an end, even though we've seen several examples exchanging hands for over MSRP in recent months. Let's just say this: mileage matters.
You know I've been keeping a close eye on these things for a while now. Not just the Raptor R, but also the C8 Corvette, all the Hellcat variants, and so on.
The "problem" with the Raptor R has always been availability. Ford dealers don't exactly have dozens of these babies sitting around waiting for customers, and securing an allocation can be difficult. Still, there's a difference between holding your value and going up in value. Let's take this particular 2026 Raptor R for example.
It was purchased new by its original owner for $117,520, driven for roughly 2,200 miles, and then listed at auction with no reserve. The winning bid turned out to be $118,000 (plus a buyer's fee), meaning the seller technically got $480 over MSRP for it. Purely from a depreciation standpoint, that's a pretty spectacular result, I don't care where you're from!
In terms of specs, this Raptor R comes with an Antimatter Blue Metallic exterior, which I think looks fantastic - especially compared to some of the more common colorways you can get on a flagship F-150. Actually, I'm not going to downplay this, because I think this color might just be my favorite Raptor R hue ever. Not gonna lie. What do you guys think about the spec?
Other highlights include the model-specific vented hood, Code Orange tow hooks, R badges, LED headlights, Rigid LED fog lights, side mirror lighting, a dual-panel sunroof, power-operated tailgate, tonneau cover, and a receiver hitch.
Meanwhile, the 17" forged beadlock-capable wheels come wrapped in BFGoodrich KO2 all-terrain rubber, while the suspension features Fox dual live-valve shocks. You also get Ford's Terrain Management System and Trail Control, so this thing is obviously more than just a straight-line beast.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Moving along to the interior, that's where you'll find the heated and ventilated front Recaro bucket seats, a heated 60/40 split-folding rear bench, Black Alcantara suede and leather upholstery, carbon fiber trim, a 14-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a wireless charging pad, a heated and leather-wrapped steering wheel, a 360-degree camera system, and more.
As for the engine, it's a supercharged 5.2-liter Predator V8 , not unlike what you'd find in a Mustang Shelby GT500 (albeit with a smaller supercharger pulley and revised software). The factory output is 720 horsepower and 640 lb-ft of torque, with everything getting sent to all four wheels via a 10-speed automatic transmission.

I guess we'll just have to wait a bit longer before we see ZR1X prices come down on the used market. Not that these things depreciate like "regular cars", but eventually, the novelty will wear off and valuations will stabilize to MSRP-levels, probably even lower at some point.
But for now, sellers are still holding out for considerably more than MSRP, and I can't say I blame them. Just last week, a Minnesota-based dealer managed to sell a ZR1X Coupe 3LZ ZTK for $107,000 over MSRP. A car pretty much identical to this one. Granted, it did come with an interesting backstory, having been used by GM as a Captured Test Fleet vehicle. But still, that's a lot of money.
Meanwhile, we've also seen more than a couple ZR1X owners refuse to sell their cars despite receiving bids/offers that were well above the original sticker price. It happened with a 2027 model year Arctic White example back in October, and now it's happened again with this black 2026MY example.
The latter was listed at auction by an Illinois-based dealer, and the bidding came to a halt at $281,000, which fell short of the reserve. The window sticker on this beauty was $247,560, which means the highest bidder was at least willing to pay an additional $33,440 on top of MSRP - a 13.5% premium on a car that's already been driven for roughly 2,800 miles.
I'm inclined to believe that's a fairly reasonable offer. This isn't some delivery-miles example that's never been registered or driven on public roads. Then again, I can also understand why the dealer decided to hold out for more. If other ZR1Xs are still fetching over $300,000 easy, why settle for $281k? The market is what it is, and prices are not quite ready yet to come down.
Anyway, let's take a closer look at the spec on this car, because it's nothing short of spectacular. Hmm, spec - spec(tacular). Never made that association before.

Expeditors International is moving into a new logistics galaxy. The Seattle-based third-party logistics provider announced Wednesday that it will handle logistics for a start-up project designed to support spacecraft launches at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Expeditors ( NYSE: EXPD ) will be the exclusive logistics provider and anchor tenant for All Points Logistics LLC, a Florida-based company technical services contractor for the government and defense industry that is developing multi-user spacecraft processing and logistics facilities at Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, to provide cleanroom processing, fueling, storage and other support services to commercial and government launch customers.
Under the long-term lease agreement, Expeditors will provide warehousing, inventory control, inbound transportation management, project cargo services, customs brokerage, supply chain visibility and distribution services for space system operators and manufacturers. The company is also expected to provide similar services in California.
In April, All Points signed an exclusive agreement with NASA for a 65-acre, 50-year lease at Kennedy Space Center to build two facilities. All Points Logistics said it plans to build a 266,000-square foot Spaceport Logistics Center on a 65-acre site at Kennedy Space Center. The facility will be located within five miles of the launch pads and is scheduled to open by the end of 2027. The site will also include an adjacent 260,000 square-foot processing center, integrating launch-site logistics and specialized spacecraft processing capabilities.
U.S. Space Force Command in July awarded All Points a $250 million contract to design and build a commercially owned Spacecraft Processing Center at Vandenberg Space Force Base.
The work is being done by All Points’ Space Prep business, which was created to develop and operate facilities payload processing, storage and other mission support for the space launch industry.
Customers will also have access to Expeditors’ broader global network, connecting suppliers and manufacturing locations with launch operations. The Kennedy Space Center location positions Expeditors to serve existing customers, including hyperscalers, as they explore opportunities in space-based data centers and advanced computing infrastructure, the company said.
“Companies in the space industry manage highly specialized equipment and materials across global supply chains,” said Ed Rone, Expeditors’ regional vice president, U.S. Southeast, in a news release. “This partnership puts our people and services closer to their launch operations, transforming logistics from a transportation function into a mission-readiness capability that helps ensure critical flight hardware, launch equipment, and operational assets are available at the right time.”
Expeditors already has a specialized line of business centered on the aerospace industry. Last summer it expanded its Aircraft on Ground service offering, which helps airlines and suppliers quickly arrange transportation for engines and other critical parts needed for aircraft repairs and maintenance.
The asset-light company had revenue of $4.1 billion during the third quarter, up 41% year over year. Operating income increased 54% to $445.4 million, with management citing high demand from AI-related companies for helping increase revenue.
All Points says that by combining private capital with targeted government investment, it will deliver scalable Infrastructure-as-a-Service capability that provides a more flexible path to more spacecraft processing capacity.
“As an independent provider unaffiliated with launch service providers or spacecraft manufacturers, we offer priority access to the Space Force, [NASA] and neutral access to others with consistent pricing,” said Kevin Brown, senior vice president at Space Prep, in a July 29 news release. “The commercial ownership and operation model frees the government from relying on scarce military construction funding while adding competition and dissimilar redundancy to the nation’s space launch industrial base.”

Spy Photos: 2027 Hyundai Porter LT2 Caught With Less Camo, Features Pleos Connect
20 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The next-generation Porter looks different from the cab-over truck we've known for more than two decades now. The latest spy photos of the 2027 model show a longer and more angular front end, complete with rectangular headlights near the outer edges. Replacing the almost vertical front profile of the Porter II, a stepped nose is on the menu as well.
LT2 is what Hyundai calls the newcomer internally, and the latest prototype is rocking a fairly small cabin that leaves plenty of room for the bed. The flatbed test vehicle is most interesting when admired from either side, for its design creates a more pronounced separation between the passenger cell and the front of the vehicle than its predecessor.
From the standpoint of styling, the simple headlight clusters flank a mostly closed panel. Whether that means the pictured vehicle is electric or not, we can't tell for certain from these photos. A more camouflaged prototype from October 2026, however, confirmed that electric muscle is coming to the Porter. Look even closer, and you will notice flatter and more angular surfacing than before.
The safety cell is mostly flat on three sides, flaunting a dramatic windshield rake for good measure. Pictured on good ol' steelies, the work-spec prototype integrates a low-height flat cargo bed with three hinged side and rear gates. Tie-down points are visible as well, and the same can be said about its rectangular taillights.
White-painted bars prevent rear window damage, as you'd expect from this kind of commercial vehicle. Regarding the reason why the LT2 looks so differently from the outgoing model, the flat-front design is gone to meet stricter frontal crash safety regs.
Moving the cabin backward behind the front wheels and adopting a semi-hood layout results in more front structure, including crumple zones, between the front bumper and the driver's legs.
Photo: SH Proshots The LT2 is expected to be sold in Europe as well, hence the safety-conscious design. A very popular truck in South Korea, the current Porter is especially popular with delivery companies and construction business. With the LT2, both electric and liquefied petroleum gas powertrains are planned. Hearsay suggests that no diesel or gasoline options are planned.
Spied last month, the more camouflaged electric prototype showed a visible charging connection and a black-painted frame with a marking that indicates four-wheel drive . In other words, the electric LT2 should offer at least one dual-motor option when it goes live in the first half of 2027.
Based on the only interior pic snapped by our carparazzo, the LT2 is also getting Pleos Connect software. You can think of Pleos Connect as the key to Hyundai's software-defined vehicle strategy. Pleos combines infotainment, cloud connectivity, vehicle control functions, and fleet management capabilities. In the world of commercial vehicles, Pleos could be incredibly useful.
Consider a delivery business that operates a bunch of LT2s. Fleet management software would help an operator monitor the fleet's condition, check maintenance schedules, coordinate servicing effortlessly, and so forth, making everyone's job easier. The wider Pleos ecosystem supports advanced ADAS, with Hyundai planning a Level 2+ rollout in the latter part of 2027.

2027 Ducati Desmo450 EDX Gets New Six-Speed Gearbox and Retuned Suspension
13 photos
Photo: Ducati
Shortly after it presented to the world the first Desmo250 EDX motorcycle in its enduro and cross-country offering, Italian bike maker Ducati saw fit to present the updated version of the older 450 EDX as well. And there's quite a bit to be excited about.
Building on the platform that came to light for the first time at the end of last year, the machine brings to the enduro-cross table a new six-speed transmission, that replaces the previous five-speed one, along with updated final-drive gearing (13/50), and a retuned Showa suspension system, tailored specifically developed for cross-country riding.
The two-wheeler continues to be based on the Desmo450 MX platform that marked the bike maker's entry in this segment in the spring of 2025, and that means it is still animated by a 449.6cc Desmodromic single-cylinder engine that delivers 64 horsepower at 9,400 rpm and 39 lb-ft of torque at 7,500 rpm.
The engine draws its energy from a new, transparent tank that can hold 2.2 gallons (8.3 liters) of fuel. It also benefits from revised starter gear tolerances, an updated water-pump seal, and a reinforced exhaust mounting point.
I mentioned earlier the suspension system tailored for cross-country activities. That was achieved by Ducati engineers through the fitting of a fully adjustable 49 mm Showa inverted closed-cartridge fork with 310 mm (12.2 inches) of travel at the front, and a fully adjustable Showa monoshock that delivers 301 mm of wheel travel at the rear.
Speaking of wheels, these are fitted with Takasago Excel aluminum rims and continue to be sized 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear. They are both shod in Pirelli Scorpion XC Mid-Soft tires to be able to handle all kinds of terrain.
The Italians throw the 2027 Desmo450 EDX onto the market complete with a lot of standard fittings, including handguards, a skid plate, and a side stand. There are a few extras that have been thrown into the mix specifically for the 2027 model year, more specifically the updated shift and rear-brake pedal tips, revised engine mounting brackets, and a reinforced chain-guide support.
The upgraded motorcycle tips the scales at 237 pounds (108 kg) and will be dressed in a revised graphics package. All the changes, says Ducati, are meant to make the Desmo450 EDX even better than it already is at taking on both tricky sections and wide-open stretches.
We're told the new bike will become available at American dealers starting early next month. It will carry a starting price of $12,495, and, just like before, it will be eligible for the Ducati Race Rewards program.
That's the Italian manufacturer's off-road racing contingency program for the United States, through which Ducati supports privateer racers competing at approved events across the country.
