source_document.body:
Logistics companies say the technology and AI they have already put to work is paying back. What they want from the next round is proof, delivered faster.
Scott Monnig, chief client officer at Sparq, said he is hearing that demand from clients. Sparq describes itself as an AI-native digital engineering services firm that re-engineers the systems businesses run on, and Monnig said many of its clients look like the companies attending FreightWaves’ F3 conference.
Sparq released its inaugural 2027 Transportation & Logistics Insights Report at F3. The company commissioned a survey of 313 U.S. decision-makers in freight brokerage and forwarding, trucking, parcel, and courier and last-mile delivery. Ninety percent said their implemented technology or AI investments met or exceeded return-on-investment expectations, while 62% require faster ROI timelines from vendors.
Monnig traced the demand for proof to the past year.
“In 2025 our customers told us and the industry was telling us that we were in a proof of concept phase, and not everybody was having a lot of success with those,” Monnig said in an interview on FreightWaves Today. “This year they’re moving into proofs of value.”
Satisfied buyers still want faster payback
The two findings overlap: among respondents whose ROI met or exceeded expectations, 61% also require faster ROI timelines from vendors, according to the report. Monnig summed up the mood as “pleased but not satisfied.”
“What they’re now pivoting to in the industry is from the question of does this work to how can you prove this works and how can you generate more return faster,” he said.
Budgets are still growing. Eighty-seven percent of respondents expect technology and AI budgets to increase next fiscal year, including 26% who expect increases of at least 20%. Those budgets come with conditions, Monnig said.
“They can’t just do it on a promise,” he said. “They have to have measurable results.”
The ROI figures are self-reported against expectations and were not independently audited, the report notes. Monnig described the survey as arm’s length by design.
“This isn’t our opinion. This isn’t the opinion of vendors in the room here. These are self-reported results from the technology decision makers,” he said.
Forty-nine percent of respondents were final decision-makers, 40% were key influencers, and 90% were director level or above. InnovateMR conducted the survey from August to September 2026.
Labor and fuel costs raise the stakes
Driver and labor costs and availability were the most-cited margin pressure in the survey at 52%, followed by fuel at 50% and insurance and liability at 43%. In trucking, the American Transportation Research Institute’s 2026 Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking put the industry-average cost to operate a truck at $2.336 per mile in 2025, up 3.4% from the previous year.
Fuel and labor costs sit somewhat beyond the reach of technology, Monnig said.
“But what the decision makers are telling us is that even though those things are beyond their control, what is in their control is tying those measurable improvements to business outcomes,” he said.
Despite those pressures, 95% of respondents are very or somewhat optimistic about growing profitably over the next 12 to 24 months.
Legacy systems lead a long list of barriers
Respondents are broadly comfortable with their data infrastructure: 39% are very confident and 55% somewhat confident it can support AI-driven decisions. Asked for the single biggest barrier to moving faster on AI or advanced data investments, 24% named legacy systems and integration, followed by data quality or availability at 19%, unclear ROI at 17%, budget constraints at 16%, and lack of internal expertise at 12%.
“It wasn’t like there’s one giant problem to solve,” Monnig said.
Even among respondents confident in their data infrastructure, 23% name legacy systems and integration as their biggest obstacle.
Monnig called connected data the foundational layer.
“In a lot of organizations today, there are silos of data, there are pockets of data, and each one may be good on their own, but what decision makers need to do is recognize that in order to get the return from AI systems, they really need to weave that data into a fabric of context,” he said.
Forecasting lags peak readiness
Ninety-two percent of respondents said they are mostly or fully prepared for the 2026 holiday peak shipping season. Forecasting is another matter: 53% picked forecasting accuracy among the three supply chain challenges they are least prepared for, ahead of cybersecurity and labor shortages. Among respondents who have already implemented demand forecasting, 52% still put it on that list.
“We can have high confidence in our ability to address peak season, but our confidence level about the forecasting system insight isn’t there yet,” Monnig said.
He tied the gap to how far ahead companies are asked to look.
“When we’re asking about peak holiday season, we’re talking two or three months,” he said. “But you ask for two or three quarters, and it’s far.”
Budgets for 2027 rest on that longer horizon.
Dispatch expected to change most
Thirty-four percent of respondents expect dispatch and operations to see the greatest technology-driven transformation over the next two to three years, ahead of sales and pricing at 21%, customer service at 18%, and finance and back office at 12%. Operations and dispatch was also the largest primary department among respondents, at 27%.
Monnig said what matters most in dispatch is the information behind each decision.
“Decisions are happening and need to happen faster every day. In order to make better decisions faster, you need more information, not necessarily more data,” he said. “You need that information, and that’s where technology systems, that data context, natural language processing, the capabilities that AI systems bring, really can bring a step change to that portion of the organization.” Learn more about Sparq and their report.

Only 15% of senior operations leaders say they’re redesigning how work gets done around artificial intelligence , even though 60% expect AI to substantially or completely change their business model within three years. The findings come from Accenture ’s latest Pulse of Change survey .
What’s Related
Nearly half of operations leaders, 47%, say they’re using AI to improve existing ways of working or to experiment without changing how the work is done. And 72% see more potential for AI to grow revenue than to cut costs.
Accenture surveyed 3,000 C-suite leaders across 19 industries and 21 countries in July and August 2026. The findings are based on responses from 392 senior leaders overseeing areas such as supply chain, procurement , production, and research and development.
RELATED STORIES: Gartner: Nearly Half of Supply Chains Cut Staff Because of AI | 10 Routine Supply Chain Tasks You Should Use AI For
Leaders expect immediate ROI
About six in 10 operations leaders (61%) expect a measurable return on AI investment within a year or less. That compares with 52% of C-suite leaders responsible for other parts of the business. Those figures reflect what executives expect to see from AI spending. The survey findings released by Accenture did not specify how respondents define a measurable return.
Seven in 10 operations leaders plan to spend more on AI over the next 12 months, and 66% say they’re tracking the cost of running AI more closely than they were a year ago. Accenture did not specify how much respondents expect to increase spending or how much of that money they plan to put toward redesigning processes.
Cybersecurity ranks high on the list
Cybersecurity was the most common choice when operations leaders were asked which strategic priority had grown in importance. Fifty-four percent pointed to strengthening their defenses and improving their ability to recover from an attack.
The level of concern varied by region. In North America, 55% of operations leaders said they were highly or extremely concerned about cyberattacks, compared with 37% in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
Most leaders still expect to hire
Even as companies plan to spend more on AI, 57% of operations leaders expect to hire more people over the next year. North America had the highest share at 67%, followed by Europe, the Middle East, and Africa at 53% and Asia-Pacific at 51%. Accenture's findings did not break down which jobs leaders expect to fill.
Tracey Countryman, Accenture’s global lead for supply chain and engineering, pointed to the challenge of using AI across the different stages of a product’s life. “What they lack is the operating model to scale it across the value chain, from a product’s first concept to how it’s engineered, made and serviced. More pilots won’t close this gap.”

In Another Pointless PR Stunt, Geely's Lynk & Co Drives the 07 GT off a Cliff To Show How Safe It Is
12 photos
Photo: @InsideChinaAuto via X
You know that car sales are bad in China when every carmaker resorts to crazy PR stunts to promote their vehicles. Geely's Lynk & Co may have gone too far in this quest by throwing its 07 GT station wagon off a cliff at 70 kph. Surprisingly, all doors can still open after the ordeal. However, it's unlikely that the fall would be survivable for anyone inside the cabin.
It's no secret that the Chinese car market has entered a tailspin, with October sales recording a 27% decline compared to 2025. Companies with a global footprint have tried their best to offload production to overseas markets. This explains why car exports have surged 60% in October. However, they could not offset the local sales slump, with the overall market still losing over 9% of combined sales (domestic and exports).
Desperate times call for desperate measures, they say. In this case, it's PR-stunt time, with Chinese carmakers racing for the craziest and goofiest demonstrations. Just yesterday, we wrote about BYD resorting to some interesting acrobatics to promote the Denza BAO 5. Specifically, the SUV proved it could tow a Boeing 747 even without two wheels, which is probably what most customers would want to do with their cars.
Now, we have Geely trying to steal the show with another act meant to promote the Lynk & Co 07 GT. Towing capacity and power were good for the Denza, but for a family car, Geely chose safety. There's no official Euro NCAP rating yet for the station wagon that debuted in Paris last month. So, what better way of proving its safety can you find, other than throwing the car off a cliff?
Photo: @InsideChinaAuto via X And so the story went, with Lynk & Co designing a ramp to thrust the 07 GT into the air and down into the abyss. During the video shared on social media, the car rolls over several times on a steep mountainside, both longitudinally and laterally. If you've seen it in movies, you'd expect the car to start throwing body parts and probably explode by the time it hit the bottom, but it didn't.
Even more impressively, all doors could still open, while the glass roof, although cracked, was still protecting the cabin. Again, exactly the scenario that every family wants to test before buying a new car. As impressive as the wreckage looked at the end of the demonstration, I seriously doubt any passenger would still be alive after so many rolls and bumps.
Chen Qu, Geely's Global Communications chief, thinks otherwise, as he reposted the video on X with the text "we have the safest car in the world." He admits that Volvo might disagree, but it's OK, because Volvo is also owned by Geely, so it's a family quarrel. We have the safest car in the world, don't argue this with me, except you @volvocars — Kevin Chen (@Geely_Kevin) November 19, 2026

Japan's 2027 BMW M3 Edition 40 Jahre Is Limited to 20 Sedans and 20 Wagons
16 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW Japan is celebrating 40 years of the M3 with a very special edition of the current generation, a special edition split between 20 units of the G80 and 20 examples of the family-oriented G81. Referred to as Edition 40 Jahre, this fellow can be had in two paint colors. Each model gets 10 examples in blue and 10 in a plum-burgundy shade, namely E46-era Laguna Seca Blue and look-at-me Wildberry.
Customer deliveries are scheduled to start later this month, and the M3 Edition 40 Jahure can only be described as pricey. The sedan carries a suggested retail price of 17,610,000 yen, with the wagon adding a further 100,000 yen over that. In other words, prepare at least 110,150 and 110,750 dollars, respectively.
Both stickers include consumption tax, yet registration expenses, insurance, and other applicable charges will make them pricier still. A separate recycling fee also needs mention. The 100,000-yen difference is most surprising if you ask me, especially when you remember how much more car you get.
Back home in Germany, the M3 Competition xDrive sedan and its equivalent Touring brother are now going for 107,600 and 108,900 euros, respectively. And that's before you account for the goodies that come by default as part of the 40th anniversary treatment.
Both models receive a black roof with M striping, 826M forged wheels in Gold Bronze, M Compound brakes with high-gloss black calipers, and plenty of carbon fiber.
Photo: BMW Fitted with 19s up front and 20-inch rear wheels, the Japanese-market special edition is rocking carbon-fiber side mirror caps, front bumper intake garnish, and carbon fiber for the rear diffuser. The deck lid spoiler of the sedan is carbon fiber as well, and saying carbon fiber this often made me remember that meme featuring Kazushige Sakamoto of Garage Active next to a custom R32 Nissan GT-R.
Hopping inside, customers will be welcomed by more *checks notes" carbon fiber in the form of body-hugging bucket seats wrapped in Silverstone Full Merino leather upholstery. Anniversary logos for the front headrests are standard as well, along with a commemorative badge on top of the cup holder cover.
Carbon fiber is the material selected by the German automaker for parts of the center console and dash, with carbon fiber extending to the steering wheel spokes and shift paddles. Dedicated M sills, a heated steering wheel, acoustic glass, M Drive Professional, and Parking Assistant Plus are standard too, plus automatic trunk lid/tailgate operation.
The Touring is the one to have if you need the additional cargo space, and between you and me, the Touring is the better-looking machine of the two as well. Regardless of body style, a twin-turbo I6 does the talking to the tune of 530 ps (523 hp) and 650 Nm (479 lb-ft) of twist.
Shipping in right-hand drive, the Japanese models come with M xDrive (featuring RWD-only mode) and an eight-speed automatic. Unfortunately, there is no manual option to speak of. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BMW Japan (@bmwjapan)

Vale’s (NYSE: VALE) base metals unit is backing a mining engineering degree at Memorial University as it looks to recruit more skilled workers for its fly-in, fly-out Voisey’s Bay nickel mine in Labrador.
The company has committed $3.9 million (US$2.8 million) and will offer co-op work placements as part of a $9-million initiative with the university and the province. Memorial aims to admit its first students in fall 2027 , pending approval of the program in mining and mineral processing.
“My life might have been very different if this program had existed 30 years ago,” Colleen Roche, Vale Base Metals’ general manager of health, safety, environment and risk in Newfoundland and Labrador, told The Northern Miner at the Mineral Resources Review in St. John’s. “I’m really excited that kids, especially kids from the Indigenous communities, will see a pathway to meaningful careers and transferable skills.”
Roche left Newfoundland to study mining engineering at McGill University in Montreal after the 1993 Voisey’s Bay discovery. Memorial wants to train students from Indigenous and rural communities for jobs in the province.

A Senate committee advanced a bill on Wednesday that would require warehouses , distribution centers , and other businesses covered by the measure to let truck drivers use existing restrooms when they pick up or deliver freight . The bill would apply while drivers wait for their trucks to be loaded and throughout a delivery, including unloading.
What’s Related
The Senate Commerce Committee advanced the bipartisan Trucker Bathroom Access Act by voice vote. Sens. Lisa Blunt Rochester, D-Del., and Deb Fischer, R-Neb., introduced the bill Nov. 12. It still needs approval from the full Senate and House before it can become law.
The bill covers commercial drivers subject to federal oversight of driving hours. It would give them reasonable access to bathrooms already set aside for employees or customers, provided that letting drivers in poses no obvious health or safety risk to the driver or security risk to the business.
RELATED STORIES: The Top 10 Issues Facing the Trucking Industry in 2026 | Ranking the Top 50 Trucking Companies in the U.S. for 2025
Who it applies to
The bill would apply to businesses that send or receive goods by truck, including manufacturers and freight facilities that are closed to the public. It also covers businesses open to the public when drivers are there for a pickup or delivery. Warehouses and other businesses covered by that part of the bill could use their existing restrooms without making physical changes. Buildings of 800 square feet or less with employee-only restrooms would be exempt.
Marine terminals would have additional obligations. They would have to provide enough restrooms for drivers hauling freight through the terminal, with portable toilets allowed where extra facilities are needed. Terminal operators would also have to give drivers a place to park their trucks while they use the restroom.
Why it matters
A pickup or delivery can leave a truck driver waiting at a customer’s facility for hours. In a 2024 report, the American Transportation Research Institute found that drivers reported waits of more than two hours at about 39% of their stops in 2023. A separate study by the institute found that 39% of women drivers surveyed cited limited or no restroom access as a daily problem, compared with 23% of men.
The American Trucking Associations backed the bill and said its Women In Motion Council had made restroom access a priority in meetings with lawmakers. On the House side, Reps. Troy Nehls, R- Texas , and Chrissy Houlahan, D-Pa., introduced a companion measure. The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee included restroom access provisions in the BUILD America 250 Act, a transportation package it approved in May.

View of the open pit at Cuiú Cuiú in Brazil. Credit: Cabral Gold.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 19, 2026
Cabral Gold (TSXV: CBR, US-OTC: CBGZF) has lifted measured and indicated gold resources by 49% to just under 1 million oz. at Cuiú Cuiú in northern Brazil, where the company poured first gold in September. The stock soared.
The estimate, effective Nov. 11, puts measured and indicated resources at 42.5 million tonnes grading 0.73 gram gold per tonne for 998,800 oz., according to a statement Thursday. Inferred resources rose 376% to 82.1 million tonnes grading 0.95 gram gold per tonne for 2.51 million oz. The estimate covers six deposits about 195 km south-southwest of Itaituba in Pará state. “All six of the deposits identified to date are open at depth, and several are open along strike,” CEO Alan Carter said in the statement.
Cabral shares jumped about 13% to $1.27 Thursday morning on the TSX Venture Exchange, valuing the company at about $441 million (US$308 million). The stock has traded between 55¢ and $1.68 in the past year.
Second phase
Most of the gold in the updated estimate lies in hard rock beneath the shallow oxide ore that feeds Cabral’s new mine.
The heap-leach operation is designed to treat 3,000 tonnes of oxide ore a day. Measured and indicated gold in that material grew 21% to 265,600 oz., while inferred ounces rose 190% to 210,900.
A planned second phase would target hard rock containing 733,200 indicated oz. and 2.3 million inferred oz., up 63% and 406%, respectively, from the 2022 estimate. The new estimate used a long-term gold price of US$3,500 ($5,005) per oz. to set the limits of the modelled pits. Cabral plans infill drilling in 2027 to move some of the inferred material into higher-confidence resource categories.
Alluvial gold
Located in the Tapajós gold district, Cuiú Cuiú covers 306 sq. km. Cabral’s Brazilian subsidiary estimates that small-scale miners recovered up to 2 million oz. of alluvial gold at Cuiú Cuiú during the region’s gold rush. The company has worked in the area since 2017. Cabral started with an open-pit mine that leaches gold from weathered rock near the surface. Its July 2025 prefeasibility study put pre-production capital at US$37.7 million and projected about 113,000 oz. of gold over 6.2 years from the oxide operation. Vancouver-based Cabral received the mine’s operating licence in August and reported its first sale of more than 2,400 oz. of gold to a Brazilian refinery in September.
It said at the time that it expected to reach commercial production by year-end. Thursday’s update said the mine was still ramping up.
Cabral also holds the Bom Jardim exploration property about 25 km northwest of Cuiú Cuiú. It controls two exploration licences covering more than 13,000 hectares in the former alluvial mining district, where it has conducted geophysical surveys, sampling and limited drilling.

He Bought a Ford Mustang Dark Horse Six Months Ago and Already Sold It for $27,000 Under Sticker
17 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Just six months. This is how long the original owner of this 2026 Ford Mustang Dark Horse spent with his brand-new car before he listed it for sale. That was because the payment turned out to be a bit too much. He is keeping the Tesla that he is Ubering because it makes him money, while the Mustang is spending it.
The man is trying to buy a house. He can no longer afford two cars. So he gave up what he calls " the most thrilling car " he has ever had because the loan payment turned out to be " a little too much " for him. It happens. He can buy one later.
"I also do Uber after work, and the Tesla makes me money, " he admits, while, with the rising gas prices, the Ford Mustang Dark Horse is only spending it in the meantime. So the time has come for him to let go of it. " It's been a very difficult decision, " he admits.
He seems to have specced the Ford Mustang Dark Horse the right way. The car is obviously dressed to kill. It is finished in Carbonized Gray Metallic over a black interior and rides on 19-inch Tarnished Dark-painted wheels.
Photo: Cars and Bids It comes with the Premium trim, which brings the leather-trimmed seats with heating and cooling, color-accented door panels and contrast stitching, a driver seat with memory, and the 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system for the moments the driver has had enough of the V8 orchestra.
Speaking of which, the 5.0-liter Coyote V8 from under the hood packs naturally aspirated firepower and pumps out 500 horsepower (507 metric horsepower) and 418 pound-feet (567 Newton meters) of torque. The numbers position it right between the GT and the Dark Horse SC .
The Mustang Dark Horse can rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.7 seconds when the auto box is involved, like in this car, run the quarter mile in 12.0 seconds with a trap speed of 118 mph (190 kph) and max out at 166 mph (267 kph). The ten-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels in pure Mustang fashion, while Brembo brakes provide the stopping power.
The man paid $69,230 to drive the Ford Mustang Dark Horse off the showroom floor back in May 2026. Six months later, he only got $42,000 for it, which caused him a solid $27,230 financial blow in just half a year.
Photo: Cars and Bids Lucky for the buyer, who got a muscle car that is still practically new, with zero modifications, only 7,100 miles on the clock, and a clean Carfax report. The buyer is also going home with two keys and the owner’s manual, along with the factory warranty valid for a total of five years or 60,000 miles, whichever comes first. Ordering a new car would mean $70,570 before any options.

source_document.body:
Amazon told New York City customers on Thursday that a proposed city law could add up to $5 per order. The company said it may consider moving delivery facilities outside the city if the bill passes.
What’s Related
The bill would require operators of certain last-mile facilities to get a city license and directly employ workers who sort and handle packages or regularly deliver them to customers, with some exceptions. Amazon told the City Council in April that the bill, as written, would end its contracts with more than 40 local delivery businesses that employ more than 5,000 people.
Councilmember Tiffany Cabán introduced the proposal, known as Intro 518 or the Delivery Protection Act, in February. The City Council’s consumer and worker protection committee held a hearing in April, and the bill remains in committee.
Who it applies to
Amazon calls the companies that deliver packages from its stations Delivery Service Partners. These businesses hire their own drivers, manage their fleets, and assign routes. Under the bill, operators of covered facilities would generally have to bring that work in-house. The hiring requirement would apply to full-time drivers and part-time drivers who do covered delivery work for more than eight hours in any 30-day period.
The direct-hire rules would take effect roughly a year after the bill becomes law. Operators could apply for extensions for qualifying contracts already in place. An extension would end when the contract expires or roughly two years after the bill becomes law, whichever comes first.
RELATED STORIES: New York City’s Delivery Boom Is Leading to More Crashes and Injuries | Amazon Delivery Vehicles Got Over 14,000 Citations in NYC
What happens to workers if contracts end
If the bill forces an operator to end a contract and the contractor lays off workers doing covered work, the operator would have to offer those workers their old jobs as direct employees before hiring anyone else. The offers would have to preserve existing employment terms and benefits.
The Teamsters pointed to a recent contract cancellation in calling for the bill’s passage. About 200 Manhattan e-bike delivery workers were affected after Amazon ended its contract with Kaizen Management Solutions this month, Streetsblog reported. Amazon told Streetsblog it ended the contract over safety issues and other breaches and was connecting affected workers with other delivery partners.
What delivery stations would need to do
Each covered location would need a two-year city license with a $500 annual fee. Operators that continue using contracted drivers under an extension would have to track their routes, verify their insurance, and post a $500,000 bond per contracted driver to cover potential court judgments from road incidents.
Amazon said moving facilities outside the city would likely mean slower and more expensive deliveries. Its notice did not name any stations it might move or say whether its current delivery partners could keep serving New York City from those locations.

November 2026 Top500 New Systems per List
The November 2026 TOP500 list has only 28 new systems, the lowest count in our tracking series going back to June 2018. This dramatic slowdown from previous editions marks a significant shift in how often the list turns over with fresh hardware.
New System Counts Hit a Series Low
Just as a quick note, the official Top500 post says there were 27 new systems, but when we filtered the list on First Appearance 68 (with 68 being the November 2026 list), we got 28 new systems. We will use these new systems for our analysis. The 28 new systems on this November 2026 list mark the lowest count in our series since June 2018, dropping from 43 in June 2026. The previous low was 39 in June 2022, and while November 2024 rebounded to 54, this edition represents a clear step down.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems per List
The June 2018 list had 133 new systems, and November 2018 had 153. Those days of roughly a quarter or more of the list turning over with each publication are long gone. Today’s 28 newcomers represent 5.6% of the full Top500.
The 28 new systems together contribute about 1.0 EF/s of Rmax, or roughly 5.1% of the list’s total performance. That is the lowest share since at least November 2021, when new systems contributed over 12%. The prior low was 5.48% in June 2023, so this continues a pattern in which even the systems that do get submitted add little aggregate HPL capability. Part of that is because LineShine was added to the list in June 2026, so a recent new #1 tends to SKU the aggregate addition numbers.
November 2026 Top500 New System Rmax Share
Only five new systems made the Top 100. The highest-ranked newcomer is KISTI’s HANGANG at #12, an HPE Cray EX254n system using NVIDIA Grace CPUs and GH200 Superchips with HPE’s Slingshot 400 interconnect. No new systems made the Top 10. LineShine remains at #1 , holding its position from the June 2026 list where it debuted with 2.198 EF/s of HPL performance using custom Arm-based LX2 processors.
With so few new systems and modest newcomer performance, total list Rmax grew from roughly 18.7 EF/s in June 2026 to approximately 19.7 EF/s now. That compares with nearly 25% growth on the previous list, which was driven largely by LineShine’s debut.
November 2026 Top500 Performance Growth Indexed
The #500 entry point rose from about 2.66 PF/s in June 2026 to roughly 2.87 PF/s now, an increase of around 8%. For context, the November 2021 threshold was just 1.65 PF/s, so the bar has been relatively low to enter the list. Just on a CPU basis, that was when a 64-core AMD EPYC 7003 “Milan” CPU was state of the art. Now, we have 256-core AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice” CPUs . CPU performance has gone up by more than a factor of four (since we get more performance per core), but we have only seen a roughly 74% increase in the “get-in” performance number.
The List Is Aging Rapidly
With only 28 new systems replacing 28 that fell off, the average system on the list has now been there for approximately 3.2 years. That is the highest in our tracking window, up from about 2.2 years in November 2021 and roughly 3.0 years as recently as June 2026.
November 2026 Top500 Average System Age
The systems that dropped off this list had been on it for an average of about 5.4 years, measured as of the current list date. That is a long tenure in terms of list appearances, and it highlights how established these departing clusters were.
There is a stark contrast between what fell off this list and what came on. Of the 28 systems that dropped, 24 were CPU-only, with most using Intel Skylake or Cascade Lake processors from roughly 2017-2019. Seventeen of the departed systems were in the Industry segment, 17 were built by Lenovo, and 14 were located in China.
November 2026 Top500 New vs Dropped Systems
By contrast, 23 of the 28 new systems are GPU- or other accelerator-accelerated. The churn is slow as well as turning over from old CPU-only commercial clusters to newer GPU-accelerated research and academic systems.
China and Industry Submissions Have Collapsed
Chinese service-provider submissions and commercial Industry clusters have nearly disappeared as sources of new entries. Systems in China fell from 173 on the November 2021 list to just 18 now. China still holds #1 with LineShine, but it has otherwise largely stopped submitting at volume. The country added only one new system this edition: CTyun HPC – shanghai15, an eSurfing Cloud entry using a MetaX C588 accelerator and China Telecom C86 CPUs.
November 2026 Top500 China and Industry Systems
The Industry segment has fallen from 258 systems in November 2021 to 146 now, and only two of the 28 new systems are classified as Industry. The rest break down as 12 Research, 12 Academic, and 2 Government.
This is the same theme we raised in our June 2023 analysis . It feels like the Top500 submissions are not a census of all HPC or AI deployments, and the commercial systems that used to populate the list have largely stopped appearing.
Who Built the New Systems
HPE leads this edition with 8 new systems and by far the most new Rmax at roughly 615 PF/s. That total is dominated by HANGANG at #12 with 342.6 PF/s and ORNL’s Lux at #14 with 220.79 PF/s, an AMD EPYC 9575F system using Instinct MI355X accelerators.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by Integrator
Lenovo has 6 new systems, MEGWARE has 4, and Dell and Fujitsu each have 3. Notably, all three of Fujitsu’s entries are Supermicro-based platforms, including the RIKYU system at RIKEN using GB200 Superchips and Nagoya University’s Flow 2.0 subsystems.
By geography, Europe leads with 11 new systems, followed by Asia with 9 and North America with 8. Germany added 6 new systems, nearly matching the United States’ 7.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by Country
South Korea has 3 new systems thanks to HANGANG and its CPU companion system at KISTI, plus a Dell PowerEdge XE9680L with B200 accelerators at Elice Inc. Japan also added 3.
CPUs: Grace Ties Intel as AMD Leads x86
Among the 28 new systems, AMD leads with 13, while NVIDIA Grace and Intel each account for 7. The remaining system uses a China Telecom C86 processor.
All five of the new CPU-only systems are AMD-based, and four of them use Turin Dense (Zen 5c) parts: HANGANG-CPU at KISTI, Manta CPU at Navy DSRC, Nagoya’s Flow 2.0 Type I subsystem, and Lichtenberg NHR-1 CPU at TU Darmstadt. The fifth, ERDC’s Barfoot, uses Genoa.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by CPU Generation
All seven new Intel systems are GPU hosts. Six use Emerald Rapids and one uses Granite Rapids. There are no new Intel CPU-only systems on this list at all, which is a notable shift for a vendor that has historically dominated the Top500. Maybe more telling is that in the latest (pre-Venice/Vera) generation, Intel has only one Granite Rapids CPU system, while AMD’s Turin has 11 systems.
Across the full list, Intel’s share has fallen to 50.2%, down from 82% in November 2021. AMD sits at 39.8%, and NVIDIA Grace now powers 6.4% of systems with 32 entries.
November 2026 Top500 CPU Vendor Share
NVIDIA Grace is the most common CPU among new systems with 7 appearances, all in GPU-host roles. Next comes the AMD EPYC 9655 with 3 systems, followed by several SKUs at 2 each, including the EPYC 9965, EPYC 9654, Xeon Platinum 8568Y+, and Xeon Platinum 8570.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by CPU SKU
The 28 new systems use 16 different CPU SKUs total. On the full list, however, the story is very different. The AMD EPYC 7763 from 2021 remains the most common SKU with 34 systems, and NVIDIA Grace is close behind at 32.
November 2026 Top500 Top CPU SKUs Full List
The EPYC 7742 has 26 systems, and the Xeon Platinum 8480+ has 20. These older models from roughly 2019-2023 still hold significant presence on this list, even as newer SKUs dominate among the latest additions.
Core Counts Split by Role
Most GPU-host CPUs have between 36 and 72 cores per socket. Grace has 72, Emerald Rapids hosts typically run 48-56 cores, and five GPU systems use 96-core EPYC parts.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by Cores per Socket
Every new CPU-only system uses a part with between 96 and 192 cores. That includes the 96-core EPYC 9654 in Barfoot, the 128-core EPYC 9745 in HANGANG-CPU, the 160-core EPYC 9845 in Manta CPU, and two systems using the 192-core EPYC 9965.
The median new system has 72 cores per socket versus 52 for the full list. Five years ago, the full-list median was just 20 cores per socket.
November 2026 Top500 Median Cores per Socket
Systems using CPUs with 24 or fewer cores have fallen from 75% of the list in November 2021 to just 19% now. None of the 28 new entries use such low-core-count processors, indicating a distinct shift in the CPU mix appearing on the TOP500.
November 2026 Top500 Cores per Socket Mix Full List
The shift toward higher core counts reflects a clear division in new system design. GPU hosts typically use moderate-core CPUs, while CPU-only systems leverage high-density EPYC parts to maximize compute throughput per socket.
Accelerators: NVIDIA Blackwell Arrives, but Hopper Is Still the Installed Base
Fourteen of the 28 new systems use NVIDIA Blackwell accelerators, split between 12 with B200 and 2 with GB200 Superchips. Hopper accounts for another 6 systems across H200, GH200, and one remaining H100.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by Accelerator
AMD has two new accelerated systems: ORNL’s Lux on MI355X at #14 with 220.8 PF/s, and C-DAC’s PARAM KAVERI in India using MI300X. MetaX has one entry with its C588 accelerator in the CTyun system.
Across the full list, accelerated systems now represent 58.6% of systems and 78.8% of Rmax. That compares with just 30% of systems being accelerated back in November 2021.
November 2026 Top500 Accelerated Share
Blackwell systems nearly doubled from 18 to 32 since the June 2026 list, while Hopper reached 137 systems. In terms of system count, AMD Instinct across all generations is still roughly at Blackwell’s level.
November 2026 Top500 Accelerator Architectures
The installed base story matters here. Even though Blackwell dominates new submissions, the full list still has more Hopper systems than anything else, and 61 Ampere-generation systems from the A100 era remain on the list.
Interconnect: InfiniBand Keeps Taking Share
Among new systems, 19 of 28 use InfiniBand. That breaks down as 14 with NDR, 2 with XDR, 2 with HDR, and one unspecified generation. Five new systems use HPE Slingshot, including the first Slingshot 400 systems on the list: HANGANG and its CPU companion at KISTI.
November 2026 Top500 New Systems by Interconnect
Four new systems use Ethernet. Two are RoCE-based, one uses NVIDIA Spectrum-X (the MEGARIDE system at CINECA), and ORNL’s Lux uses HPE Juniper with AMD Pensando 400G Ethernet.
Half of the new systems run 400Gb/s per port, and two run 800Gb/s XDR InfiniBand. These are nominal per-port line rates rather than achieved throughput, but they show where high-end cluster networking is heading.
Across the full list, Ethernet has fallen from 45% of systems in November 2021 to just 18% now. The old 10/25/100GbE commercial clusters that drove those numbers have largely aged off the list. InfiniBand now sits at 60% and Slingshot at 15%.
November 2026 Top500 Interconnect Share
InfiniBand leads new submissions with 19 of 28 systems, while Ethernet accounts for only 4. Across the full list, InfiniBand has grown to 302 systems versus 88 for Ethernet and 73 for Slingshot, showing a clear shift in the reported interconnect mix.
Final Words
The November 2026 TOP500 shows a list with limited turnover, featuring only 28 new systems and roughly 5% performance growth. The average tenure of listed systems has approached 3.2 years, marking the slowest update rate in our tracking window. China’s presence dropped to 18 systems from 173 in November 2021, while the Industry segment fell to 146 from 258. Of the new entries, 23 are accelerators.
New hardware on the list highlights specific architectural trends: Blackwell accelerators appear in 14 systems, all CPU-only newcomers use AMD EPYC processors, and NVIDIA Grace matches Intel’s count among new entrants. The Top500 remains a useful gauge for tracking declared HPL system configurations and platform trends over time. However, it does not capture the full scope of current HPC and AI compute investments, which often prioritize different benchmarks or deployment models.

NHTSA Reviews Petition Alleging 2020 Hyundai Palisade A/C Compressor Pulley Failures
36 photos
Photo: Hyundai
When the compressor of the HVAC system begins to struggle doing its job as intended, that means a little more than an uncomfortable cabin. Per a recent petition filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a failed compressor pulley and hub assembly also compromises the windshield defogging system, impairing driver visibility.
Defect petition DP26013 concerns the 2020 model year Hyundai Palisade. The Office of Defects Investigation is currently deciding whether to grant or deny the request for a formal defect investigation. Preliminary documentation identifies no fewer than 80,418 potentially affected vehicles produced for the US market.
The ODI lists four incidents, and the problem isn't entirely new. A quick search on your favorite search engine reveals that Hyundai Motor America issued technical service bulletin 25-HA-003H in August 2025 to address A/C compressor pulley issues. Applicable vehicles include the 2020 through 2025 model year Palisade assembled between April 2019 and May 2024.
Said bulletin reads that certain vehicles may experience reduced air-con performance, with Hyundai Motor America blaming an out-of-spec air conditioning compressor pulley and hub assembly. The compressor pulley service kit, a.k.a. part number 97640-S8500FFF, includes the disc and hub assembly, pulley, clutch magnetic coil, clutch bolt, and two snap rings.
Dealers were instructed to first inspect the pulley, checking for internal drag by rotating the center hub. In case of excessive drag, or if the hub is completely stuck, the compressor pulley service kit goes in at no charge to affected customers. The already documented issue, however, may pose a safety risk.
Photo: Hyundai Only the NHTSA can decide whether it can also be considered a safety risk, and this brings us back to DP26013. The compressor of an A/C unit circulates refrigerant through the system, allowing it to remove moisture and heat from the air. That moisture-removal function prevents condensation from building up on the inside of the windshield, and the system also manages fresh air intake.
The owner's manual for the 2020 model year Palisade instructs drivers to use the A/C when selecting the windshield defogging feature. If a compressor doesn't operate as intended because of a malfunctioning pulley and hub assembly, condensation is certain to build up. A foggy windshield is, from my point of view, exactly what you don't want on a rainy commute, let alone on a wintry drive.
Even while maneuvering at low speeds, one has to consider the increased risk of hitting parked cars and pedestrians. Four reports aren't much compared to the estimated population of 80,418 vehicles, yet the absence of reported injuries doesn't automatically settle a potential visibility-related safety concern.
The redesigned Palisade has had a few problems of its own, with the NHTSA listing three recalls from January 2026 through March 2026. The first one was caused by a software error that led to a failure of the instrument panel display. The second was caused by second- and third-row power seats that may fail to detect a person during powered folding or tilt-and-slide operations.
As for the final safety recall reported thus far, certain second-generation Palisade sport utility vehicles may experience third-row seatbelt buckle wiring damage. In case of damage, the vehicle may show the subject belts as permanently buckled even when unseated.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 19, 2026
Asante Gold (TSXV: ASE; US-OTC: ASGOF) opened a strategic review after receiving unsolicited approaches ahead of a month-end deadline for the Ghana gold producer to secure at least $100 million (C$143.3 million) in new funding. The stock rose.
The approaches are non-binding, Asante said Wednesday after the close of trading. It gave no terms and didn’t name the interested parties.
Executives will explain Asante’s turnaround plan for the Bibiani and Chirano mines Friday at 8 a.m. Toronto time, bringing forward a briefing originally planned for January. The company expects to appoint advisers shortly.
“An expanded main pit could allow us to access mineralization currently planned for underground mining and potentially defer significant development capital,” acting CEO Campbell Baird said of Bibiani when Asante released its quarterly results last week.
The urgency extends beyond the Nov. 30 funding deadline. Asante had $64 million in cash and a $309.7-million working capital deficit at Sept. 30. It disclosed a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on its ability to continue as a going concern.
Asante shares rose 4.5% to 35¢ Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$314 million ($220 million). The stock has traded between 14¢ and C$2.33 over the past year.
Bibiani strain
The strain is greatest at Bibiani, where all-in sustaining costs hit $7,681 per oz. in the third quarter against a realized gold price of $3,873 an ounce. Power cuts, a shortage of contractor equipment and resettlement delays hurt output. A second contractor is clearing waste after a January pit-wall failure. Asante expects to reach ore there again in the first quarter of 2027.
Asante withdrew its 2026 production and cost forecasts last week. Its financing partners have extended the funding deadline several times. Failure to meet key performance indicators under a lender-approved technical action plan would trigger a default under the company’s senior debt facility.
The withdrawal reverses an August outlook for 275,000 to 300,000 gold-equivalent oz. of annual production at all-in sustaining costs of $3,200 to $3,600 per ounce. Management had expected a stronger second half, weighted towards the fourth quarter, as Bibiani gained access to higher-grade ore, and had deferred or cancelled about $50 million in planned capital spending.
Crushing constraints
Chirano delivered 34,420 gold-equivalent oz. in the September quarter, supported by higher-grade ore from Aboduabo. That compared with 25,612 oz. in the three months ended Oct. 31, 2025. Its all-in sustaining costs were $3,722 an ounce.
At Bibiani, an independent plant review completed in September identified crushing and grinding as the main performance constraint. Mobile crushers used after the original primary crusher was taken out of service produced feed poorly suited to the mill, undermining grinding and gold recovery. Asante is working on plant stability and backup power.
Baird became acting CEO in May after joining as chief operating officer in March. The finance team also changed: David Wiens resigned as chief financial officer effective Aug. 14, and deputy CFO Dindiok Chialin became interim finance chief.
On Monday, Asante detailed an 8,000-metre at Bibiani to test the Bridge area and nearby targets. Results will inform an updated resource model and mine plan examining whether a larger open pit could defer underground spending planned for 2027 and 2028.
